P0E00.title: Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0E00.description: P0E00 is the general circuit code for the current sensor in phase U of the generator. Each phase sensor, usually a Hall-type device inside the inverter, outputs a voltage around a mid-point when no current flows. No manufacturer documents P0E00 publicly. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV shows how its generator unit judges the U-phase sensor: at standstill below 20 rpm with the IGBTs off the signal must stay between 2.3 and 2.7 V (P0E01-00 after 0.32 s), and readings of 0.5 V and lower, or 4.5 V and higher, held for 0.2 s set P0E02-00 or P0E03-00. P0E00 is meant for circuit faults outside these categories. Without the signal the inverter cannot regulate generator torque properly. Phases V and W are P0E04 and P0E08.

causes.label: Supply or reference fault of the current sensor
Defective phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Faulty internal connection between sensor and control board

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and engine warning light
Generator switched off, reduced performance
Vehicle may not reach ready mode

P0E01.title: Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0E01.description: P0E01 flags an implausible zero point of the U-phase current sensor inside the generator inverter. Sensors of this kind put out a voltage near the middle of their span while no current flows, so the test is only run when the machine cannot carry current. Mitsubishi documents the code for the Outlander PHEV: on the 2023 model the generator control unit evaluates the U-phase signal with the IGBTs switched off, the generator turning below 20 rpm and at least 8 V supply, and stores P0E01-00 if the value leaves the 2.3 to 2.7 V band for 0.32 s; MIL and hybrid warning light come on. The 2018 code chart calls the same code an offset fault of current sensor 1. A shifted zero distorts generator torque control. Hard signal faults of this sensor appear as P0E02 or P0E03.

causes.label: Zero point of the phase U current sensor drifted (sensor inside the power drive unit)
Unstable sensor supply or reference voltage inside the inverter
Evaluation circuit of the generator control unit faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator output reduced, less charging while driving
Code often returns after clearing at the next standstill check

P0E02.title: Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0E02.description: P0E02 is stored when the output of the generator inverter's phase U current sensor falls to the bottom of its range, a level no real current would produce. Mitsubishi uses it on the Outlander PHEV: from model year 2023 the generator control unit, supplied with at least 8 V, sets P0E02-00 once the U-phase signal drops to 0.5 V or lower and stays there for 0.2 s; unlike the zero-point test, no standstill is needed. The 2018 code chart describes the same code as a ground short or a broken line at current sensor 1. Because the sensor is built into the power drive unit, Mitsubishi's procedure ends with replacing that unit after a confirming drive cycle. The offset check is P0E01, the opposite fault P0E03. Without a valid U-phase value the generator usually runs only in a limited way.

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to ground or sensor output failed low
Open signal or supply connection of the sensor inside the power drive unit
Input stage of the generator control unit faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator power limited or generator not used
Battery charge falls faster in hybrid operation

P0E03.title: Generator Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0E03.description: P0E03 is the upper-limit fault of the current sensor that measures phase U of the generator inverter: its signal is pinned near the supply rail. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi lets the generator control unit set P0E03-00 when the U-phase voltage climbs to at least 4.5 V and remains there for 0.2 s with the unit supplied by at least 8 V; for the 2018 model the code list blames a short to the supply or a shorted current sensor 1. A reading this high would mean a phase current far beyond anything the generator delivers, so the controller treats it as an electrical defect and not as overcurrent; genuine overcurrent has codes of its own, at Ford for instance P0A71. On the 2023 model the MIL is switched on as well. Low signal: P0E02, zero-point fault: P0E01.

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to its supply voltage
Current sensor in the power drive unit failed with high output
Lost sensor ground or reference inside the inverter

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator switched off or strongly limited
Engine runs more often without charging the battery

P0E04.title: Generator Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0E04.description: P0E04 is the general circuit code for the generator inverter's V-phase current sensor, meant for an electrical fault that is not narrowed down to offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents P0E04 publicly. Phase V is a special case: the 2018 Outlander PHEV measures generator current with only two sensors, on phases U and W (P0E01 to P0E03, P0E09 to P0E0B), since the third current follows arithmetically from the other two. Only the 2023 model adds its own V-phase sensor, and there its faults are reported solely through P0E05 to P0E07. CARB requires electrical monitoring of hybrid components that affect emissions. If the code does appear, check the inverter connectors and look for further phase sensor codes. Matching codes for phases U and W: P0E00 and P0E08.

causes.label: Electrical fault in the V-phase sensor circuit inside the inverter
Poor contact at the inverter or generator control unit connector
Generator control unit faulty

symptoms: Hybrid or engine warning light on
Reduced generator output

P0E05.title: Generator Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0E05.description: P0E05 reports an implausible zero point of the current sensor in phase V of the generator inverter. Mitsubishi describes it only for the 2023 Outlander PHEV, the first of its generator units with a sensor in phase V; the earlier model measured just U and W. The test mirrors that of the other phases and runs at rest: IGBTs off, generator below 20 rpm, control unit fed with at least 8 V. If the V-phase signal then sits outside 2.3 to 2.7 V for 0.32 s, P0E05-00 is logged and the MIL turns on. As no current can flow in this state, any deviation points to the sensor itself. A zero error left in place would also disturb the three-phase sum check P0DFA, so both codes may appear together. Open or shorted signals of this sensor are P0E06 and P0E07.

causes.label: Zero point of the phase V current sensor drifted
Disturbed sensor supply or reference in the power drive unit
Generator control unit evaluation faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Possibly also the phase sum code P0DFA stored
Less generator support during hybrid driving

P0E06.title: Generator Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0E06.description: P0E06 means the phase V current sensor of the generator inverter delivers a signal at the floor of its range. The 2023 Outlander PHEV is the only documented user: Mitsubishi's generator control unit, running on 8 V or more, stores P0E06-00 when the V-phase voltage remains at 0.5 V or below for 0.2 s, and the MIL comes on. Electrically this fits an interrupted signal or supply line or a signal shorted to ground, which is how Mitsubishi's older chart explains the matching U-phase fault. On this model the sensor is integrated in the power module, so the official remedy after a confirming test drive is a new unit. The older Outlander PHEV has no V-phase sensor and therefore never sets P0E06. Related: P0E05 (offset) and P0E07 (signal high).

causes.label: V-phase sensor signal shorted to ground or sensor failed low
Open sensor signal or supply inside the power drive unit
Input of the generator control unit faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator power limited

P0E07.title: Generator Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0E07.description: P0E07 is set when the phase V current sensor in the generator inverter reports a signal stuck high. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV has its generator control unit flag P0E07-00 as soon as the V-phase voltage is at 4.5 V or above for 0.2 s while its own supply is at least 8 V; MIL and hybrid warning both illuminate. Real current cannot cause such a value, so the fault lies in the sensor, a short to its supply or in the evaluation circuit. The earlier Outlander PHEV, which measured only phases U and W, has no counterpart. When several phase sensors report high at the same moment, a shared supply problem inside the unit is a more likely explanation than three separate defects. Siblings for phase V: P0E05 (offset) and P0E06 (low).

causes.label: V-phase sensor signal shorted to its supply
Common sensor supply in the power drive unit too high or faulty
Current sensor failed with high output

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator switched off or limited
Other phase current sensor codes stored at the same time

P0E08.title: Generator Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0E08.description: P0E08 covers an electrical fault of the generator inverter's W-phase current sensor that falls outside the offset, low and high categories. No manufacturer documents P0E08 publicly. Unlike phase V, the W-phase sensor exists on both Outlander PHEV generations Mitsubishi describes: the 2018 model uses it as current sensor 2, the 2023 model as one of three, yet both log its faults only as P0E09, P0E0A and P0E0B. CARB demands circuit monitoring of hybrid components relevant to emissions. A sensor that delivers no usable value at all keeps the inverter from controlling generator torque, so the system will typically cut generator power and rely more on the engine or the battery. Phase U counterpart: P0E00, phase V: P0E04.

causes.label: Electrical fault in the W-phase sensor circuit inside the inverter
Loose or corroded connector at the power drive unit
Generator control unit faulty

symptoms: Hybrid or engine warning light on
Reduced generator output, battery charged less while driving

P0E09.title: Generator Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0E09.description: P0E09 is the zero-point check of the phase W current sensor in the generator inverter. Mitsubishi uses it on two Outlander PHEV generations. The 2018 code chart lists it as an offset fault of current sensor 2, the second of only two generator current sensors. For 2023 the generator control unit runs the same standstill test as for U and V: IGBTs off, generator under 20 rpm, at least 8 V supply, and the W-phase voltage has to stay inside 2.3 to 2.7 V; 0.32 s outside that band sets P0E09-00 and the MIL. On a two-sensor layout an offset in W also corrupts the V current derived from it, so control quality suffers on two phases at once. Hard signal faults of the same sensor are P0E0A and P0E0B.

causes.label: Zero point of the phase W current sensor drifted
Sensor supply or reference in the power drive unit unstable
Evaluation in the generator control unit faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Rough or reduced generator operation
Fault reappears at the next standstill check after clearing

P0E0A.title: Generator Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0E0A.description: With P0E0A the phase W current sensor of the generator inverter reports a signal at or near zero volts. Mitsubishi covers this code in its Outlander PHEV service information: the 2018 chart attributes it to a short to ground or an open circuit of current sensor 2, and in the 2023 model the generator control unit sets P0E0A-00 after the W-phase voltage has stayed at 0.5 V or lower for 0.2 s with at least 8 V supply, lighting the MIL. On the 2018 two-sensor layout, losing phase W leaves a single measured phase, too little for current control, so generator operation is heavily restricted. Mitsubishi's procedure first deals with codes of higher priority, confirms the fault with a drive cycle and then replaces the power drive unit. Related: P0E09 and P0E0B.

causes.label: W-phase sensor signal shorted to ground or sensor failed low
Open sensor signal or supply inside the power drive unit
Input stage of the generator control unit faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator largely out of operation
Battery is charged noticeably less while driving

P0E0B.title: Generator Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0E0B.description: P0E0B marks a phase W current sensor signal in the generator inverter that sits at the top of its range. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi's generator control unit records P0E0B-00 when the W-phase voltage stays at no less than 4.5 V over a period of 0.2 s with a supply of at least 8 V, and turns on the MIL; the 2018 code chart names a short to the supply or a short circuit of current sensor 2. A value like this would match a current well above the generator's capability, so it is judged as a sensor fault, not as overcurrent, which Mitsubishi handles separately with P30A3. The code concerns the W-phase sensor alone; an open phase winding or cable shows up as P0E0C instead. Lower-limit and offset faults of this sensor: P0E0A and P0E09.

causes.label: W-phase sensor signal shorted to its supply voltage
Current sensor in the power drive unit failed with high output
Lost sensor ground or reference inside the inverter

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator switched off or limited

P0E0C.title: Generator Phase U-V-W Circuit/Open
P0E0C.description: P0E0C concerns the three power phases between generator inverter and generator, not the current sensors. The J2012 title fits the use Mitsubishi documents for the 2023 Outlander PHEV under its own label of generator current deviation: with at least 50 A commanded, the generator between 500 and 4,500 rpm and 8 V supply, a U, V or W current stuck within about 17 A either side of zero for 0.4 s, or a failed comparison with the target current, sets P0E0C-00 and the MIL. A phase that carries no current despite a demand is just what an open line looks like; GM checks drive motor phases in a similar way under P0C05. Likely causes are loose high-voltage terminals, a damaged phase cable or winding, or the inverter. Phase sensor faults are P0E00 to P0E0B.

causes.label: Loose or burnt high-voltage phase terminal between inverter and generator
Phase cable or generator winding interrupted
Power drive unit does not drive one phase (switch or driver fault)

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning light on
Generator no longer charges, engine runs without series hybrid support
Possible noise or vibration from the generator under load

P0E0D.title: Generator Phase U-V-W Circuit Low
P0E0D.description: P0E0D is the low member of the generator phase circuit group: a U, V or W line between inverter and generator is pulled toward the negative high-voltage rail or to ground, for instance through damaged insulation or a lower power switch that conducts when it should not. No manufacturer documents P0E0D publicly. From this trio, Mitsubishi's generator unit in the Outlander PHEV only uses the open-circuit code P0E0C and catches dangerous currents with its own code P30A3; for the comparable drive motor trio GM's hybrid tables use only P0C05. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid components. A low phase usually goes together with overcurrent or insulation warnings, so an insulation test of cable and winding belongs in the diagnosis. High counterpart: P0E0E.

causes.label: Phase cable or winding insulation damaged, leakage to ground
Lower IGBT of one phase leaking or shorted
Phase voltage evaluation in the inverter faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light, possibly with insulation fault message
Generator shut down

P0E0E.title: Generator Phase U-V-W Circuit High
P0E0E.description: P0E0E reports a generator phase line that reads high: one of the U, V or W connections is held near the positive high-voltage potential, typically by an upper power switch that stays on or by a short to the positive rail. No manufacturer documents P0E0E publicly; the generator units Mitsubishi describes for the Outlander PHEV only use P0E0C here, and in GM's tables only the open-phase check P0C05 is used for the corresponding drive motor group. CARB still requires circuit faults of hybrid components to be detected. Because a phase stuck high lets current flow without control, inverters normally shut the gate drive off at once; the generator then stops supplying charge and the vehicle runs with restricted hybrid function. Low and open counterparts: P0E0D, P0E0C.

causes.label: Upper IGBT of one phase shorted or not switching off
Phase line shorted to the positive high-voltage rail
Phase monitoring in the inverter faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator shut down, no charging while driving

P0E0F.title: Generator Inverter Power Supply A Circuit/Open
P0E0F.description: P0E0F is set when the generator inverter loses one of its internal supplies, supply A, or the line to it is interrupted. Which supply carries the letter A is up to the manufacturer; usually it is the low-voltage feed of the gate drivers that switch the power transistors. No manufacturer documents P0E0F publicly. The drive motor counterpart P0C0B shows how such a check works at GM: the IGBT module itself reports a bias fault once its gate drive supply drops below a threshold, which the 2011 Volt treats as Type A after a single 2.08 ms event and a 2019 table after 0.168 s within a 0.2 s window. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid components. Without gate drive supply the generator cannot be controlled at all. Low and high variants: P0E10, P0E11; supply B: P2CC5.

causes.label: Gate driver supply inside the inverter failed
12 V feed, fuse or connector of the inverter interrupted
Deep 12 V dips during start-up

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator out of operation, vehicle may not reach ready state

P0E10.title: Generator Inverter Power Supply A Circuit Low
P0E10.description: P0E10 means supply A of the generator inverter is present but too low. Ford lists the code in the HEV OBD system summary for its power-split hybrids (OBDSM1901): in the paragraph on the gate signal lines of motor and generator, P0E10 appears with P0BCE and P0BCF among the generator-side open-circuit faults, while the motor side is covered by P0C0C. For Ford, P0E10 is therefore tied to the gate drive path of the generator inverter rather than to a separate supply part, and no voltage limit is published. CARB requires circuit monitoring for such hybrid components. A weak gate drive supply can leave the power switches only partly turned on so they overheat, which is why the inverter limits or stops the generator. Siblings: P0E0F and P0E11.

causes.label: Gate drive supply or gate signal path in the inverter faulty (Ford)
Low 12 V supply to the inverter, e.g. weak battery or poor ground
Corroded or loose inverter connector

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator limited or switched off, reduced hybrid performance

P0E11.title: Generator Inverter Power Supply A Circuit High
P0E11.description: P0E11 is stored when supply A of the generator inverter is above its permitted range. Overvoltage on the gate driver feed can overstress the control inputs of the power transistors, so controllers usually react by blocking the inverter. No manufacturer documents P0E11 publicly. Ford's hybrid summary shows that such supplies are watched: a gate drive power supply above 15.08 V counts as a fault there, though Ford files it under a rotor position circuit voltage check and not under P0E11. CARB asks for circuit fault detection on hybrid parts. A short between two supply rails or a faulty regulator inside the inverter are the likely causes; a charging system fault on the 12 V side can also contribute. Siblings: P0E0F and P0E10; supply B high: P2CC7.

causes.label: Voltage regulator of the gate driver supply in the inverter faulty
Short between two internal supply rails
Overvoltage in the 12 V system (DC/DC converter or charging fault)

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Generator blocked, no charging while driving

P0E12.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater A Control Circuit/Open
P0E12.description: P0E12 concerns the command circuit of battery coolant heater A, the electric element that warms the coolant sent to the hybrid or EV battery when the pack is too cold for charging or full power. The controller flags it when this circuit is open or otherwise electrically faulty. No manufacturer documents P0E12 publicly. GM's 2016 Volt shows the same check under its own code P1EC3: above 10.2 V system voltage, 20 failed readings within 40 samples taken every 100 ms set a Type B code. CARB requires every electronic output used to heat the energy store to be checked for circuit faults. Typical finds are a cracked conductor, an unseated connector or a dead output stage. In frost the car may then limit charging or rely on the engine. Shorts to ground or voltage are P0E13 and P0E14.

causes.label: Broken or chafed wire in the heater A command circuit
Loose, corroded or unlocked connector at the heater or controller
Open circuit inside the heater A assembly
Failed output driver in the controlling module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Slow or reduced charging in cold weather
Engine runs more often than usual on cold days
Reduced electric power until the pack warms up

P0E13.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Low
P0E13.description: P0E13 is the low-signal case on the command line of battery coolant heater A: the controller reads the line near ground at a moment when it expects a higher level, which points to a short to ground or a driver that cannot pull the circuit up. No manufacturer documents P0E13 publicly. GM's 2016 Volt folds open circuit, ground short and voltage short of its battery heater transistor into the single code P1EC3, rated Type B. Keep this low-voltage command fault apart from an isolation fault of the high-voltage heater element: GM bulletin PIC5920B lists the battery heater of the 2011–2014 Volt and 2014 ELR as one possible cause of isolation codes. CARB requires circuit checks on battery heating outputs. With the heater stuck off, winter charging slows down. P0E12 is the open circuit, P0E14 the high case.

causes.label: Command wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed against the body
Moisture or coolant in the heater connector
Internal short in the heater's control input
Output driver in the controller stuck low

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery heater does not work at low temperatures
Longer charging times in winter

P0E14.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater A Control Circuit High
P0E14.description: P0E14 is logged when heater A's control wire sits too high, typically because it touches a supply voltage or because a pulled-up input has lost its connection. No manufacturer documents P0E14 publicly; GM's 2016 Volt reports open, ground and voltage faults of its heater transistor together as P1EC3 (Type B). The high case deserves care because, depending on the design, a line held at supply voltage can keep the heater energised against the controller's will. Heater makers guard against that: a patent now held by PTI EV Hybrid describes a battery coolant heater with a thermistor in its housing that cuts power when the coolant warms faster than a set rate. CARB requires circuit monitoring of battery heating outputs. P0E13 is the low counterpart, P0E12 the open circuit.

causes.label: Command wire shorted to a supply or neighbouring live wire
Open connection on a pulled-up heater input reading as high
Output driver in the controller that will not switch off

symptoms: Check engine light on
Heater shut down by its own overheat protection
Battery heating unavailable or erratic in cold weather

P0E15.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater A Control Performance
P0E15.description: P0E15 means heater A can be addressed electrically but does not deliver the heat it was asked for. Stellantis uses the code on Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrids from 2017 onward and the 2021–2023 Jeep Wrangler 4xe for the high-voltage electric coolant heater (ECH), a LIN-controlled unit that on these models heats the cabin loop. The ECH locks itself after low or high voltage, lost communication or overheating; repeated overheating locks it until service or, on the Wrangler after the third event, for good, and P0E15 must be present for the reset routine. Causes named are coolant leaks, air, frozen or wrong coolant, a faulty auxiliary pump, supply problems or the heater itself. Several bulletins (08-052-22, 08-080-26) cure false or permanent P0E15 entries with HCP/AHCP software. The MIL comes on and EV mode may be lost.

causes.label: Low coolant, leaks or trapped air in the heater loop
Hybrid control software that needs an update (Stellantis HCP/AHCP)
Heater unit permanently locked or internally failed
Faulty auxiliary coolant pump or restricted hoses
High- or low-voltage supply fault or LIN bus problem at the heater

symptoms: Check engine light on
Message that electric mode is unavailable, engine keeps running
Little or no heat from the electric heater
Permanent code may block an emissions inspection

P0E16.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater B Control Circuit/Open
P0E16.description: P0E16 is the open-circuit code for a second battery coolant heater, B. Why a car has two: some thermal systems pair the pack heater with another heater, for example one for the cabin loop, and can route its heat to the battery. A patent from Magna E-Car describes exactly that fallback when the battery pack heater fails, so the letter depends on how the maker splits the heaters. No manufacturer documents P0E16 publicly, and none of the GM, Ford or Stellantis papers checked used it. The logic matches heater A, which GM's 2016 Volt checks as P1EC3 with 20 failures in 40 samples (Type B). CARB requires circuit monitoring of each output used to heat the energy store. Look for a broken wire, a loose connector or an open element. P0E17 and P0E18 are the shorts.

causes.label: Broken wire in the heater B command circuit
Loose or corroded connector at heater B
Open element or electronics inside heater B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery warms up slowly in cold weather
Reduced charging power at low temperatures

P0E17.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater B Control Circuit Low
P0E17.description: P0E17 reports that the command signal to battery coolant heater B stays too low, most often from a short to ground between controller and heater. No manufacturer documents P0E17 publicly. Some designs give the second heater a different job, such as warming the cabin loop, and only borrow it for the pack when needed, as a Magna E-Car patent outlines; the wiring of heater B may then run through other areas than that of heater A. GM covers ground shorts of its battery heater command inside the broader code P1EC3 on the 2016 Volt (Type B), so an exact low-only threshold is not public. CARB requires circuit checks on heating outputs of the energy store. Chafing near brackets and water in the plug are the classic finds. Open circuit is P0E16, short to voltage P0E18.

causes.label: Heater B command wire shorted to ground
Water or coolant in the heater B connector
Internal short at the control input of heater B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Second heater does not support battery warm-up
Slower charging in winter

P0E18.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater B Control Circuit High
P0E18.description: P0E18 says the command line of battery coolant heater B reads high when the controller expects it low, for example from contact with a supply wire or an interrupted pulled-up input. No manufacturer documents P0E18 publicly. The risk here is a heater that cannot be switched off. Many coolant heaters therefore carry their own guard; one patent design with a thermistor in the heater housing stops current when the coolant temperature climbs faster than a limit. GM's 2016 Volt groups voltage shorts of its battery heater command into P1EC3 (Type B). CARB requires circuit monitoring of energy-store heating outputs and, where possible, a functional check of heating. A pinched wire against a live feed or a driver that sticks on is typical. Short to ground is P0E17, open circuit P0E16.

causes.label: Heater B command wire shorted to a voltage source
Controller driver stuck on
Interrupted pulled-up input at heater B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Heater B switched off by its overheat protection
Battery heating unavailable in cold weather

P0E19.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Heater B Control Performance
P0E19.description: P0E19 means heater B is commanded and electrically intact but the expected warming does not follow. No manufacturer documents P0E19 publicly. How such a test works is visible in GM's 2016 Volt, where the battery heater performance code P1EC6 runs once per drive or charge: during an active heat request the pack inlet coolant must gain more than 3 °C within 154.1 s, otherwise a Type B fault is stored; it is skipped while coolant level or inlet temperature sensor codes are active. CARB asks for such a functional check of heating where feasible. Air in the loop, a weak pump, a blocked hose or a failing element are the usual causes, and a wrongly routed valve can send the heat elsewhere. Unlike P0E15 for heater A, this concerns the second heater. P0E16 to P0E18 are its circuit codes.

causes.label: Air pocket or low coolant level in the battery loop
Heater B element producing too little heat
Weak pump, restricted hose or coolant valve in the wrong position
Inlet coolant temperature sensor reading wrongly

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery stays cold for a long time after a cold start
Reduced charging and drive power in winter

P0E1A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P0E1A.description: P0E1A reports an open or otherwise faulty command circuit for battery coolant pump B, a second electric pump found where the battery loop is split or a separate circuit feeds a chiller or heater. No manufacturer documents P0E1A publicly. For pump A, GM's 2019 tables show how the controller judges such a line by current: while running, below 200 mA or above 3 A is a fault, while off, below 120 µA; failing for 4 s within a 5 s window gives a Type B code. A second pump would usually be monitored the same way. CARB requires every electronic output of battery thermal management to be checked for circuit faults. Usually a wire has parted, a connector has backed out or the pump itself is dead. The low and high cases are P0E1B and P0E1C; supply and speed faults of pump B have their own codes, P2CF4 to P2CF7.

causes.label: Broken wire in the pump B command circuit
Loose or corroded connector at pump B
Failed electronics inside pump B
Failed pump output in the controlling module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery or electronics temperatures rise faster under load
Reduced power or charging rate

P0E1B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P0E1B.description: P0E1B narrows a pump B command fault down to a level below the expected window, normally because the control or PWM wire has a ground fault, or because a driver that cannot raise it. No manufacturer documents P0E1B publicly. The nearest documented relative is P0C48 for pump A, which Ford listed for the 2020 Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Lincoln Aviator hybrids and traced to battery energy control module software that is reprogrammed. A software cause of that kind is worth ruling out first before cutting into the harness. Physically, a low reading often comes from insulation rubbed through on a bracket or from coolant wicking into the connector. CARB wants each thermal management output checked for such faults. If pump B stops as a result, the loop it serves loses flow. Open circuit is P0E1A, short to voltage P0E1C.

causes.label: Pump B control or PWM wire shorted to ground
Coolant or water in the pump connector
Control module software fault, as seen by Ford on the pump A sibling
Internal short at the pump B control input

symptoms: Check engine light on
Pump B does not run
Power limited when the components it cools get hot

P0E1C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P0E1C.description: P0E1C is set when the command signal to battery coolant pump B stays above what the controller allows, for instance because the line is shorted to battery voltage or, on a pulled-up PWM input, interrupted. No manufacturer documents P0E1C publicly. Its pump A counterpart P0C49 appears in Ford bulletin 20-2293 for the 2020 Lincoln Aviator hybrid among MIL codes for the coolant pumps, with BECM reprogramming as the fix. In contrast to a ground short, a line held high can either keep a simple on/off pump running continuously or, with PWM pumps that read a steady high as an invalid command, make the pump fall back to a default speed or stop. CARB requires circuit monitoring of thermal management outputs. Look for a wire touching a live feed. P0E1B is the low case, P0E1A the open circuit.

causes.label: Pump B control wire shorted to battery voltage
Interrupted pulled-up PWM input at the pump
Control module software fault, as Ford found for pump A

symptoms: Check engine light on
Pump B runs constantly or not at all
Reduced power under heavy load

P0E1D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Control Performance
P0E1D.description: P0E1D says pump B accepts its command electrically but the effect the controller looks for does not appear, such as the expected flow, speed or temperature change in its loop. No manufacturer documents P0E1D publicly. The model is pump A on the 2011 Chevrolet Volt: once the pump has run for over 60 s, the pack inlet coolant temperature must have shifted by at least 5 °C, otherwise a Type B code is set. GM bulletin PI0798A traces that pump A code after a drain and refill to trapped air, cleared with a vacuum purge, which is also the first check for pump B after service work. CARB calls for a functional check of battery cooling where feasible. Worn bearings, a clogged inlet or a sensor reading wrongly are further causes. Pump B speed faults may also show as P2CF6 or P2CF7.

causes.label: Air trapped in the loop after a coolant service
Worn pump B or debris blocking its impeller or inlet
Low coolant level or leak in the battery loop
Coolant temperature sensor giving an implausible value

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery or electronics temperatures higher than normal
Gurgling noise from the coolant loop
Power or charging rate limited

P0E1E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0E1E.description: P0E1E does not describe the wire or the pump directly but the switching stage that drives pump B: that driver has reported excess current or overheating and has protected itself. Such smart switches measure their own state; a TI automotive high-side switch, for example, turns off at about 150 °C junction temperature or on reaching its current limit and signals the fault on a diagnostic pin. No manufacturer documents P0E1E publicly. GM's 2019 tables show a comparable monitor for a different load, the fuel pump driver code P1255: a board temperature of 160 °C or more, 3 failures in 15 samples, Type B. A pump that drags or seizes, a partial short in the motor or a hot mounting spot of the module are typical. Pump A has the same code as P0E1F.

causes.label: Pump B binding or seized, drawing too much current
Partial short in the pump motor or its wiring
Driver in the module overheating due to location or poor cooling
Degraded output driver in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Pump B switches off intermittently
Battery or electronics temperature rises, power is limited

P0E1F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0E1F.description: P0E1F reports that the output stage switching battery coolant pump A has hit its current or temperature limit. Ford uses the code on its 2020 hybrids. On the Escape HEV built up to 10 June 2020, bulletin 20-2221 lists P0E1F in the battery energy control module beside pump and battery codes and blames strategies in the BECM software, fixed by reprogramming PCM and BECM. Bulletins 20-2293 and 20-2345 name it for the Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Aviator hybrids, with the MIL on and a BECM update as the cure. If software is ruled out, the hardware logic applies: smart switches such as TI's automotive high-side parts shut off at their current limit or around 150 °C and report the event. A stiff pump, a short in the motor or a heat-soaked module remain. Pump B has the same code as P0E1E.

causes.label: Battery energy control module software (Ford 2020 hybrids)
Pump A binding or seized and drawing excess current
Partial short in the pump motor or harness
Output driver overheating in the module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Battery coolant pump stops intermittently
Hybrid power limited when the battery gets warm

P0E20.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Control Valve A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0E20.description: P0E20 points at the driver that powers coolant control valve A: its output has exceeded a current limit or run too hot and switched itself off. No manufacturer documents P0E20 publicly. Valve A is often a small motor actuator; on the 2011 Chevrolet Volt it is driven in both directions through two drive lines, each with its own ground and voltage short checks (90 failures in 100 samples at 6.25 ms, Type B). Driving a motor into a jammed end stop is exactly what heats such a stage, so a sticking valve is a prime suspect. Mercedes reports the electrical fault of its battery shutoff valve as P0CDF00 instead. TI's automotive smart switches illustrate the protection itself: shut-off at the current limit or near 150 °C, with a fault flag. P0E21 and P0E22 cover valves B and C.

causes.label: Valve A sticking or jammed so the actuator stalls
Partial short in the valve actuator motor or its wiring
Degraded valve driver in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Valve A stays in its last position
Battery runs too warm or too cold, power or charging limited

P0E21.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Control Valve B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0E21.description: P0E21 is the overload or overheat report of the driver for coolant control valve B. No manufacturer documents P0E21 publicly. What B means differs between makers: on the 2011 Chevrolet Volt, GM's own codes for valve B (P1EC7, P1EC8) actually watch the second drive line of the same valve motor that serves as valve A, whereas other layouts have a physically separate second valve for a chiller or radiator branch. For diagnosis it is therefore worth checking first which actuator the maker calls B. The protection itself works like that of TI's integrated high-side switches for cars, which cut off at their current limit or near 150 °C and report it. CARB obliges makers to monitor these outputs electrically. Electrical circuit faults of valve B are P0D1A, P0D1D and P0D1E.

causes.label: Valve B binding so its actuator stalls against the stop
Short or low resistance in the valve B actuator or harness
Degraded driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Coolant routing does not change as commanded
Battery temperature drifts, power or charging limited

P0E22.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Control Valve C Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0E22.description: P0E22 tells that the driver for a third coolant control valve, C, has protected itself against excessive current or heat. No manufacturer documents P0E22 publicly, and none of the reviewed GM, Ford, Stellantis or Mercedes documents uses a valve C at all. Three valves suggest a loop with several branches, for example radiator, air-conditioning chiller and heater, with C switching one of them. Unlike a plain ground short (P0DEB), the overload code catches a load that still conducts but draws too much, so a stiff valve or a shorted turn in its motor is the likely trigger rather than a broken wire. CARB requires that every electronic output of battery thermal management be checked for circuit faults; TI's automotive smart switches show the mechanism: they disconnect once current reaches the limit or the junction nears 150 °C.

causes.label: Valve C stiff or jammed by deposits
Shorted turn in the valve C actuator motor
Degraded driver stage in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
One branch of the coolant loop no longer switches
Battery overcooled in winter or kept too warm in summer

P0E23.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit
P0E23.description: P0E23 is the catch-all circuit code of drive motor inverter temperature sensor G, a thermistor that watches the power switches of the motor inverter. It stands for an electrical fault the controller cannot pin down as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents P0E23 publicly. The only published user of the G series is Mitsubishi: in the 2023 Outlander PHEV the seventh IGBT sensor of the front motor unit (U-phase H2) reports its faults as P0E24, P0E25 and P0E26, but not as P0E23. CARB requires hybrid input components to be tested for open circuits and out-of-range signals. Without a valid temperature the inverter is usually run with reduced torque; the sensor sits inside the inverter, so repair often means that assembly.

causes.label: Temperature sensor or sensing board inside the inverter failed
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector
Faulty evaluation input in the motor control unit

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light and MIL on
Reduced electric drive power

P0E24.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Range/Performance
P0E24.description: P0E24 is the plausibility test of inverter temperature sensor G: the signal is electrically fine, but the temperature it reports does not fit. Mitsubishi uses the code on the 2023 Outlander PHEV for IGBT sensor number 7 in the front motor control unit, labelled U-phase H2. The check runs only after a soak of at least 600 s, with the IGBTs shut down and the unit fed with 8 V or more, within 1.5 s of these conditions being met. Should it then deviate from either of two other IGBT temperatures by more than 47 °C for 0.1 s, P0E24-00 is logged; MIL and plug-in hybrid warning light both light up. After a long stand all switches should be equally warm, so the code points to a drifting sensor. Mitsubishi's flow ends with a new power drive unit.

causes.label: Sensor G reads offset against the other IGBT sensors
Fault on the sensing circuit of the power drive unit
Uneven inverter cooling, e.g. air in the coolant circuit

symptoms: MIL and plug-in hybrid warning light on
Often no noticeable change in driving

P0E25.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Low
P0E25.description: P0E25 means the voltage of inverter temperature sensor G has fallen below its valid window. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi assigns it to the U-phase H2 sensor of the front motor control unit and sets P0E25-00 once that signal does not rise above 1.25 V during 0.08 s with a unit supply of 8 V upward; the MIL is switched on together with the hybrid warning lamp. Mitsubishi states only the voltage. For an NTC element fed through a pull-up resistor, as GM describes for its inverter sensors, a low voltage equals a very hot sensor, so a ground short or a damaged sensing line looks like an overheated switch. Real overheating is reported by separate temperature codes. The opposite limit is P0E26; the sensor is not sold separately.

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to ground inside the inverter
Thermistor internally shorted
Damaged sensing board, e.g. after coolant ingress

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning light on
Motor power limited as if the inverter were overheating

P0E26.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit High
P0E26.description: P0E26 is logged when the signal of inverter temperature sensor G climbs above its permitted range. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV it belongs to the front motor unit's U-phase H2 sensor: at least 3.75 V lasting 0.08 s, with at least 8 V supply to the unit, sets P0E26-00 together with MIL and hybrid warning light. With an NTC element and pull-up resistor, the layout GM documents for its inverter thermistors, such a voltage would mean an extremely cold power switch, which a working inverter never shows; the usual reasons are an open sensing line, a lost reference ground or a broken thermistor. The low-side fault is P0E25. Because the sensor is built into the unit, Mitsubishi replaces the power drive unit.

causes.label: Open sensing line or broken thermistor
Lost sensor reference ground
Signal shorted to the sensor supply

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning light on
Reduced electric drive power as a precaution

P0E27.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0E27.description: P0E27 marks short dropouts or jumps in the signal of inverter temperature sensor G. Between the events the reading is normal again, which is what separates it from the steady faults P0E25 and P0E26. No manufacturer documents P0E27 publicly; Mitsubishi, the one documented user of sensor G on the 2023 Outlander PHEV, checks that sensor for plausibility and for both voltage limits only. CARB expects hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored for circuit faults, which covers unstable signals as well. Likely sources are a connector with poor contact, a cracked solder joint on the sensing board or a thermistor with unstable resistance. The code can vanish before the workshop sees it, and the drive may be limited while it is active.

causes.label: Intermittent contact at an inverter connector
Cracked solder joint on the sensing board
Thermistor with unstable resistance

symptoms: Warning light that comes and goes
Brief drops in electric drive power

P0E28.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit
P0E28.description: Sensor H is the eighth temperature sensor of a drive motor inverter, and P0E28 is its general circuit code for an electrical fault without a more precise low, high or erratic finding. No manufacturer documents P0E28 publicly. Mitsubishi, whose 2023 Outlander PHEV is the documented user of the H series, calls the part FMCU IGBT temperature sensor 8 (V-phase H2) and files its faults under P0E29, P0E2A and P0E2B; the general circuit code is not listed. Which component carries letter H is up to each maker. CARB requires hybrid input components to be checked for interruptions and for readings outside their range. When the value is missing, the controller has to protect that phase by limiting torque; the sensor is part of the inverter assembly.

causes.label: Sensor H or its sensing board in the inverter failed
Connector or internal wiring fault in the inverter
Evaluation input of the motor control unit faulty

symptoms: Hybrid warning light and MIL on
Limited motor torque

P0E29.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit Range/Performance
P0E29.description: With P0E29 the controller doubts the reading of inverter temperature sensor H although its voltage is valid. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV Mitsubishi uses it for IGBT sensor 8 of the front motor unit, the V-phase H2 position. The cold-start comparison is the same one used for sensors 1 to 7: soak of 600 s or more, IGBTs off, supply at least 8 V, test window of 1.5 s; a difference above 47 °C to either of two reference IGBT temperatures, held for 0.1 s, stores P0E29-00 and lights the MIL and the hybrid warning light. A sensor that is wrong by that much after a cold soak is offset, not overheated. The sibling for the U-phase sensor is P0E24. Mitsubishi verifies it on a test drive before installing a new power drive unit.

causes.label: Sensor H offset against the other IGBT sensors
Measuring circuit in the power drive unit faulty
Uneven cooling of the inverter

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning light on
Driving usually unaffected

P0E2A.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit Low
P0E2A.description: P0E2A reports that inverter temperature sensor H delivers a voltage below its lower limit. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV assigns the code to IGBT sensor 8 (V-phase H2) of the front motor control unit, triggered by a voltage at or under 1.25 V lasting 0.08 s while the supply is 8 V or higher; the MIL comes on. Sensor 8 is the last one with a generic code there: for sensors 9 to 12 Mitsubishi falls back on its own P301x codes, since the generic list stops at H. If the circuit is an NTC divider of the type GM documents, low voltage reads as excessive heat, so a ground short makes the inverter look overheated and power is cut back. Genuine phase overheating is a separate code; the high-side fault is P0E2B.

causes.label: Signal of sensor H shorted to ground
Shorted thermistor element
Moisture or coolant damage on the sensing board

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning light on
Power reduction similar to an overheating inverter

P0E2B.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit High
P0E2B.description: P0E2B is the upper-limit fault of inverter temperature sensor H. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV, where sensor H is IGBT sensor 8 at the V-phase H2 position of the front motor unit: a signal reaching 3.75 V for 0.08 s while the unit receives 8 V or more sets P0E2B-00, and the function list shows MIL and hybrid warning light for it. In an NTC circuit with pull-up, as GM uses in its inverters, the controller would read this as an implausibly cold phase, so the cause is almost always electrical: an interrupted signal path, a missing sensor ground or an element that has gone open. Its low-side partner is P0E2A, the U-phase counterpart P0E26. The repair at Mitsubishi is a new power drive unit.

causes.label: Interrupted signal path of sensor H
Missing sensor ground
Thermistor element gone open

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning light on
Drive power may be limited

P0E2C.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0E2C.description: P0E2C covers an unsteady signal from inverter temperature sensor H: it flickers, jumps or drops out for moments and then recovers. That pattern differs from P0E2A and P0E2B, where the voltage stays beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents P0E2C publicly. Mitsubishi watches its sensor 8 on the 2023 Outlander PHEV only for plausibility and the two voltage limits and gives no erratic code for it. CARB's monitoring rules for hybrid input components include such intermittent faults. In practice the trigger tends to be mechanical, such as vibration at a connector, a fine crack in the sensing board or a terminal with corrosion. Freeze frame data and wiggle tests help, since the fault may be gone when the car arrives.

causes.label: Connector contact affected by vibration
Corroded terminal in the sensor circuit
Hairline crack in the sensing board

symptoms: Intermittent warning light
Occasional short power reductions

P0E2D.title: Internal Control Module Hybrid/EV Battery Monitor Performance
P0E2D.description: P0E2D is an internal self-test result of the module that supervises the high-voltage pack: the part that measures cell voltages, usually a dedicated monitor chip with its own converter and reference, does not behave as expected. It casts doubt on the measurement itself, not on a cell. Battery monitor patents such as Renesas US9735567B2 show the kind of checks involved, for example self-diagnosis of the A/D converter, detection of a broken sense line between cell and chip, or a second, simpler fault monitor. No manufacturer document on an official server explains P0E2D. CARB requires computers and hybrid components feeding the drive to be monitored. Without trusted cell voltages the pack cannot be shielded from over- or undercharge, so power is limited or the car will not get ready.

causes.label: Cell monitoring circuit in the battery control module faulty
Software error in the battery control module
Interrupted cell voltage sense line

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL on
Reduced power or vehicle not ready to drive

P0E2E.title: Battery Charger A Fuse
P0E2E.description: P0E2E concerns the high-voltage fuse that protects the branch from the battery to on-board charger A. Battery managements usually judge such a fuse by comparing the voltage ahead of and behind it, as Volvo describes for its HV fuses. Audi documents P0E2E00 for the 2022 Q5 plug-in hybrid: the hybrid battery regulation module J840 stores it intermittently with symptom code 28733, often next to P0A95, and the driver sees an electrical system fault message or the car does not start. According to Audi, a diagnostic irregularity during very dynamic cornering creates the entry without a real defect; replacing the switching unit, as guided fault finding suggests, does not help, a software update does. A truly open charger fuse stops AC charging. P0A95, P0E2F and P0E30 cover other HV fuses.

causes.label: False entry from the battery management software (Audi Q5 PHEV)
Fuse opened after a short in the on-board charger or its cable
Faulty voltage measurement at the fuse

symptoms: Electrical system fault message
No AC charging or vehicle does not start

P0E2F.title: High Voltage Fuse B
P0E2F.description: P0E2F says the battery management has found a second high-voltage fuse open, or believes it has. Several makers use it. Mercedes calls it electrical fuse B, the battery-internal fuse protecting auxiliary HV consumers in its plug-in hybrids: a shorted belt starter-alternator or another short in that line blows it, the engine no longer starts and only electric driving remains; once the short is fixed, the 2024 bulletin for series 206, 223, 254 and 290 has the HV battery replaced. On EQB models a DC/DC wake-up fault can set it without a blown fuse. Porsche lists it as fuse 2 on the 2020-22 Taycan, which is then not ready to drive. Volvo and Polestar compare the voltages after the front and rear fuse outputs with pack voltage. Main fuse: P0A95.

causes.label: Short circuit in an HV consumer on the protected branch
False detection by the battery management or DC/DC wake-up fault
Faulty voltage measurement behind the fuse

symptoms: Engine does not start, electric driving only (plug-in hybrids)
Vehicle not ready to drive or propulsion warning
MIL or HV drive system warning on

P0E30.title: High Voltage Fuse C
P0E30.description: P0E30 is the code for a third fuse in the high-voltage system, after A (P0A95) and B (P0E2F). No manufacturer documents P0E30 publicly. How such a fuse is checked can be seen from the siblings: Volvo and Polestar have the battery control module compare the voltage measured after each fuse output with the pack voltage, and Porsche numbers its Taycan fuses as fuse and fuse 2 under P0A95 and P0E2F. A pack with only two fused branches never sets P0E30. What the third fuse protects, for example a heater, compressor or charger branch, is decided by the maker. If it opens, the consumers on that branch lose power; a blown fuse normally follows a short circuit that has to be found before the fuse or the battery unit is replaced.

causes.label: Short circuit in a consumer on the third fused branch
Faulty voltage measurement behind the fuse
Software error in the battery control module

symptoms: HV system warning message
Consumers on the affected branch without function

P0E31.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A Circuit
P0E31.description: P0E31 is the general circuit code of voltage sensor A in a DC/DC converter, the measurement the converter or its controller uses to regulate output voltage. It is used for electrical faults that do not fit the low, high or erratic categories. P0E31 itself is not documented publicly by any manufacturer. GM's 2025 engine tables use the neighbouring codes for the same sensor in a converter that steadies the 12 V supply during engine auto-starts: P0E33 below 1 V, P0E34 above 28 V, P0E32 for implausible values. FCA names sensor A as voltage sensor 1 on the 2021 Ram 1500 eTorque. CARB wants open circuits and out-of-range signals of such inputs reported separately where feasible. With a lost voltage signal the converter tends to stop or run in a fallback mode.

causes.label: Voltage measurement inside the DC/DC converter failed
Wiring or connector fault on the converter
Poor ground connection of the converter

symptoms: Warning light and possibly 12 V battery warning
Engine auto-stop disabled or reduced 12 V supply

P0E32.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A Range/Performance
P0E32.description: P0E32 flags a voltage reading of DC/DC converter sensor A that is electrically valid but does not match a reference. GM's 2025 engine tables (25OBDG03A, ECM) apply it to a converter that holds the 12 V supply steady during auto-starts: in bypass mode the raw output voltage may differ from the ECM run/crank voltage by no more than 2 V, and Type B (two trips) follows once 320 of 400 samples, taken every 12.5 ms, fail. During an auto-crank 8 of 16 samples with at least 6.6 V battery voltage count, as do more than 2 failed auto-cranks out of 3. FCA's flash 08-037-21 for the 2021 Ram 1500 eTorque turns P0E32-00 into a one-trip code. Mercedes ties P0E32FA in the HV converter of S-Class hybrids to sporadic red 12 V messages.

causes.label: Voltage measurement in the converter drifting
Voltage drop on supply, ground or reference wiring
Control software needing an update (FCA, Mercedes)
Weak 12 V battery distorting the comparison during cranking

symptoms: MIL on after two trips (GM)
Red 12 V warning message (Mercedes)
Auto stop/start unavailable

P0E33.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A Low
P0E33.description: P0E33 means the controller reads an implausibly low value from voltage sensor A of a DC/DC converter, typically because the signal wire is shorted to ground. GM documents it in its 2025 engine control tables (25OBDG03A) for a converter that keeps the 12 V network stable while the engine restarts automatically: the raw voltage value 1 must drop below 1 V, and 320 failing samples out of 400 taken every 12.5 ms, about four seconds, are needed. The test runs with at least 6.6 V battery voltage in run/crank or accessory mode. GM rates it Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. P0E34 is the opposite case on the same sensor, P0E38 the matching fault on sensor B. Start-stop and the 12 V support can be limited.

causes.label: Sensor signal wire chafed through to ground
Voltage measurement inside the converter failed
Moisture in the converter connector bridging to ground

symptoms: MIL on after two trips (GM)
Auto stop/start no longer available
Possible 12 V voltage dips during engine restarts

P0E34.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A High
P0E34.description: With P0E34 the controller sees a voltage on sensor A of the DC/DC converter that is too high to be real, which points to the signal being shorted to a battery feed or another live wire. In GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03A) the ECM flags it when raw voltage value 1 exceeds 28 V, far above anything a 12 V converter output should reach. Sampling and confirmation mirror the low case: 320 of 400 readings must fail, battery voltage must be 6.6 V or more, and as a Type B fault it needs two trips before the MIL lights. A real overvoltage of the converter would not normally reach that value, so the wiring and the sensing path come first. Low readings on the same sensor use P0E33; sensor B has P0E39 for the same fault.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to a battery feed or other live circuit
Lost reference ground of the measurement, signal floats high
Faulty measuring circuit in the converter

symptoms: MIL on after two trips (GM)
Engine auto-stop disabled

P0E35.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P0E35.description: P0E35 is reserved for a voltage sensor A signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of staying wrong: the reading is erratic, but not low or high long enough for P0E33 or P0E34 to mature. No manufacturer documents P0E35 publicly. The neighbouring GM codes for the same sensor (25OBDG03A, a converter backing up the 12 V network during engine auto-starts) show the frame: valid readings lie between 1 V and 28 V and are sampled every 12.5 ms. CARB expects input faults to be split into circuit, out-of-range and, where feasible, rationality checks; an erratic code captures the unstable signal in between. Loose terminals, a cracked solder joint or a ground that only fails under vibration are the usual suspects, so the fault may come and go.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminal in the converter connector
Ground connection that fails under vibration
Cracked solder joint in the converter's measuring circuit

symptoms: Warning light that appears and disappears
Start-stop works only now and then

P0E36.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor B Circuit
P0E36.description: P0E36 is the catch-all circuit code for the second voltage measurement of a DC/DC converter, sensor B. Where a converter reads both its input and its output, or monitors one rail twice, the second path gets the letter B; FCA names it voltage sensor 2 on the 2021 Ram 1500 eTorque. No manufacturer documents P0E36 itself in public sources. GM's 2025 engine tables treat sensor B through its sibling codes only: below 1 V is P0E38, above 28 V is P0E39, and a gap of more than 2 V to the ECM run/crank voltage is P0E37. P0E36 is left for electrical faults that fit none of those, such as an open line the controller recognises as such. CARB asks for circuit faults of inputs to be detected separately where feasible. Converter output may be reduced.

causes.label: Open sense wire or unplugged connector
Second measuring path inside the converter failed
Poor ground of the converter

symptoms: Warning light, possibly 12 V battery warning
Start-stop disabled or converter output reduced

P0E37.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor B Range/Performance
P0E37.description: P0E37 says that voltage sensor B delivers a believable number which nevertheless disagrees with what the vehicle measures elsewhere. GM's 2025 engine tables (25OBDG03A) check raw voltage value 2 of the converter against the ECM run/crank voltage: in bypass mode a gap above 2 V counts, and 320 failed samples out of 400 at 12.5 ms set a Type B code. During an automatic engine restart the converter stabilises the 12 V supply, and then 8 of 16 samples are enough. FCA, which calls this channel voltage sensor 2, changed the code from a two-trip to a one-trip code with flash 08-037-21 for the 2021 Ram 1500 eTorque. Drift in the measurement, voltage drop on wiring or outdated software are typical; hard shorts are P0E38 and P0E39.

causes.label: Second voltage measurement in the converter drifting
Voltage drop on supply or ground wiring distorting the comparison
Controller software needing an update (FCA eTorque)

symptoms: MIL on, after one or two trips depending on maker and software
Start-stop unavailable

P0E38.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor B Low
P0E38.description: P0E38 is stored when the second voltage reading of the DC/DC converter, sensor B, sits at the bottom of its scale. GM uses it in the 2025 engine tables (25OBDG03A) with the same limits as on sensor A, only applied to raw voltage value 2: under 1 V, confirmed by 320 of 400 samples taken at 12.5 ms intervals and only checked at 6.6 V battery voltage or more. GM's description calls it a test for short to ground, and the result is Type B with the MIL on the second trip. Because GM uses two independent paths, a fault on just one of them points to that path's wiring or circuit rather than the converter output itself. Sensor A's low code is P0E33; P0E39 covers sensor B reading too high.

causes.label: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Failed second measuring circuit in the converter
Bent or corroded pin in the converter connector

symptoms: MIL on after two trips (GM)
Auto stop/start inhibited

P0E39.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor B High
P0E39.description: P0E39 reports that sensor B of the DC/DC converter reads far too high, a pattern GM attributes to a short to battery. The 2025 engine tables (25OBDG03A) set the bar at more than 28 V for raw voltage value 2, again needing 320 failing samples within 400 at 12.5 ms and a battery voltage of at least 6.6 V, with Type B confirmation over two trips. If only sensor B shows the excess while sensor A and the ECM's own run/crank reading stay normal, a wiring fault on the B path is far more likely than a converter that really puts out such a voltage. A lost reference ground can also let the signal float upward. Sensor A's high code is P0E34; a low reading on sensor B is P0E38, an implausible but valid one P0E37.

causes.label: Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire
Open reference ground letting the signal float high
Failed measuring circuit for sensor B

symptoms: MIL on after two trips (GM)
Start-stop switched off

P0E3A.title: DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic
P0E3A.description: P0E3A covers an unsteady signal from voltage sensor B of a DC/DC converter: short spikes, dropouts or noise that never last long enough for the hard low or high codes. Publicly, no manufacturer documents P0E3A. For orientation, GM's 2025 engine tables (25OBDG03A) accept 1 to 28 V on raw voltage value 2 and only set P0E38 or P0E39 after roughly four seconds out of five of continuous failure, so brief disturbances slip past those tests. FCA calls this channel voltage sensor 2 on the Ram 1500 eTorque. CARB wants inputs checked for circuit, range and rationality faults; an erratic code is the gap filler. A fault confined to sensor B while sensor A is steady narrows the search to the B wiring and its terminals, often in a spot that moves with the engine.

causes.label: Harness rubbing intermittently where it moves with the engine
Poor terminal tension in the sensor B circuit
Electrical interference on an unshielded sense line

symptoms: Sporadic warning light, sometimes cleared on its own
Start-stop unavailable from time to time

P0E3B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Coolant Pump Overspeed
P0E3B.description: P0E3B indicates that the electric pump circulating coolant through the high-voltage battery turns faster than commanded. A pump that suddenly spins too freely has usually lost its load, because it is moving air instead of coolant after a leak, a low reservoir or a poorly bled system. No manufacturer documents P0E3B publicly. GM's 2019 hybrid tables (19OBDG01) show how such a check works under a maker-specific code (P19FF): the controller filters the difference between commanded and reported pump speed and flags a deviation in either direction; if the pump is meant to be off but still reports over 250 rpm, that counts as well, all as Type B. The sibling P0E3C covers a pump that is too slow. Battery cooling may be reduced and charge or power limited.

causes.label: Low coolant level or leak, pump running partly dry
Air left in the battery loop after a repair
Faulty pump electronics or speed feedback signal

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced charging or drive power when the battery warms up

P0E3C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Coolant Pump Underspeed
P0E3C.description: P0E3C is set when the battery coolant pump stays below the speed it has been asked for. GM documents it specifically for the 2024–25 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray: the battery energy control module (K16) stores P0E3C, and the ECM may add P0A7B to switch on the MIL. Bulletin 24-NA-160 traces it to air collecting in the hoses next to the pump after an earlier repair; the pump halts to protect itself, which the module reads as underspeed. The fix is to lower the pump below the other plumbing and have a scan tool spin it for a quarter of an hour at 4,000 rpm, topping up the 1.9 litre loop, and to repeat if needed. Only if the code returns after two or more purges is the pump itself diagnosed. Overspeed of the same pump is P0E3B.

causes.label: Air trapped around the pump after earlier service (GM 24-NA-160)
Worn pump bearing or debris slowing the impeller
Low supply voltage or poor ground at the pump

symptoms: MIL on, with P0A7B stored in the ECM (Corvette E-Ray)
Electric front-axle drive limited when the battery gets hot

P0E3D.title: Control Pilot Indicator Control Circuit Low
P0E3D.description: P0E3D concerns the lamp or LED that shows the state of the pilot connection to the charging station, not the pilot signal itself. Low means the driver circuit reads too little voltage, typically because the line to the LED is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents P0E3D publicly. GM's Volt tables for 2011 and 2012 (11OBDG01, 12OBDG01A) fold this case into the older open-circuit code P0D2B: a ground short is detected while the LED is commanded on, with 12 failed samples out of 15 at one sample every 100 ms, Type B. The current code set gives the ground short its own code, while P0E3E takes the short to voltage. The indicator stays dark or wrong, charging normally continues. Pilot line faults are P0CF3 and P0CF4.

causes.label: Wire to the indicator LED shorted to ground at the charge port
Shorted LED or indicator unit
Faulty output driver in the controlling module

symptoms: Pilot indicator stays dark when it should light
Charging itself usually unaffected

P0E3E.title: Control Pilot Indicator Control Circuit High
P0E3E.description: P0E3E is the high-side counterpart for the control pilot indicator circuit: the module senses voltage on the LED line when there should be little or none, the classic sign of a short to a supply wire. Publicly, no manufacturer documents P0E3E. On the Chevrolet Volt, GM's 2011 and 2012 tables still handle this under P0D2B, as a second case checked while the LED is commanded off, where 40 of 50 readings, one per 100 ms, have to fail. Shorts to voltage tend to come from chafed wiring at the charge port, where several feeds run side by side, or from a failed driver stage. The LED may glow permanently or flicker regardless of the real pilot state. P0E3D is the low case, P0D2B the open circuit; charging is normally not blocked.

causes.label: Indicator wire chafed against a supply wire near the charge port
Output stage in the module stuck on
Water in the charge port connector bridging pins

symptoms: Pilot indicator lit or flickering without reason
Misleading charge port light while charging works

P0E3F.title: Charge Status Indicator A Control Circuit Low
P0E3F.description: P0E3F reports that the output feeding charge status indicator A sits too low in voltage. That light confirms to the owner that the vehicle is charging, and the expected cause is an LED line touching ground. No manufacturer documents P0E3F publicly. GM's Chevrolet Volt tables for 2012 (12OBDG01A) still count this situation under P0D2C: the ground short is looked for while the LED is commanded on, and 40 failing samples out of 50, one every 100 ms, confirm it as Type B. Newer code sets split it off as P0E3F, with P0E40 for the short to voltage and P0D2C left for the open circuit. The charge status light stays dark, so the owner cannot tell at a glance whether charging has started, though the charger itself keeps working.

causes.label: LED supply wire pinched or chafed to ground
Charge status LED shorted internally
Failed driver in the controlling module

symptoms: Charge status light stays off during charging
Charging continues normally

P0E40.title: Charge Status Indicator A Control Circuit High
P0E40.description: P0E40 is logged when the drive circuit of charge status indicator A carries voltage although the light is commanded off, typically because the line touches a live wire. P0E40 has no public documentation from any manufacturer. In GM's 2012 Volt tables (12OBDG01A) this is the second case inside P0D2C: with the LED switched off, the hybrid controller looks for a short to battery and needs 40 bad samples out of 50 at 100 ms. A light that glows while nothing is charging, or keeps glowing after charging has ended, is the visible result and can mislead the owner about the charge state. Suspects are wiring near the dash or charge port, water in a connector or a driver stage that no longer switches off. P0E3F is the low case on the same light.

causes.label: Indicator wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit
Output driver no longer switching off
Moisture bridging pins in the indicator connector

symptoms: Charge status light on although nothing is charging
Owner misled about the actual charge state

P0E41.title: Charge Status Indicator B Control Circuit Low
P0E41.description: P0E41 refers to a second charge status light, indicator B, whose driver circuit is pulled too low, usually by a short to ground. Which light carries the letter B is the maker's choice; a lamp at the charge port alongside the dashboard light would be a typical pair. No manufacturer documents P0E41 publicly, and the GM Volt and ELR tables only cover indicator A. By analogy with GM's P0D2C test on light A (12OBDG01A), a ground short would be checked while the LED is commanded on, with 40 of 50 samples at 100 ms. Because indicator B usually sits in the exposed charge port area, a pinched harness or water ingress there deserve the first look. Indicator A keeps working if only B is affected. The open-circuit code for B is P0DE5, the high case P0E42.

causes.label: Indicator B wire pinched to ground near the charge port flap
Water ingress into the charge port light assembly
Shorted LED in indicator B

symptoms: Second charge light (e.g. at the port) stays dark
Main charge indicator and charging unaffected

P0E42.title: Charge Status Indicator B Control Circuit High
P0E42.description: P0E42 means the driver circuit of charge status indicator B shows voltage at a moment when the light should be switched off, pointing to a short to a supply wire or a driver that stays on. P0E42 appears in no public manufacturer document. Indicator A gives the reference: on the 2012 Chevrolet Volt, GM's table 12OBDG01A includes in P0D2C a check for a short to battery while the LED is off, requiring 40 out of 50 failed readings at 100 ms intervals. The same logic would apply to light B. In practice indicator B often belongs to the charge port, so wet or corroded contacts and harness damage at the flap are common starting points. Expect a second light that glows or flickers out of turn. Low is P0E41, open is P0DE5.

causes.label: Indicator B wire touching a live wire at the charge port
Wet or corroded contacts bridging to a supply pin
Output driver for indicator B stuck on

symptoms: Second charge light glowing or flickering when not charging
Charging itself works

P0E43.title: Hybrid/EV Powertrain Control Module B
P0E43.description: P0E43 is the module-B counterpart of P0A1D: it reports that a second hybrid/EV powertrain controller has detected an internal failure or can no longer be trusted. Vehicles with two such processors, for example GM's Bolt EV with a second powertrain module labelled K114B (HPCM2), are where the letter B makes sense. No manufacturer documents P0E43 publicly. The A code shows what is meant: GM's 2013 hybrid tables store P0A1D when a status message from motor control processor A reports a controller failure in 3 of 4 counts, Type B, and Ford's 2019 hybrid summary uses P0A1D when the serial link between its processors fails, checked continuously. CARB requires the MIL for computer faults that impair OBD. Reprogramming or module replacement is likely; power may be limited.

causes.label: Internal processor or memory fault in module B
Software fault curable by reprogramming
Supply, ground or internal bus fault at the module

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode

P0E44.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense E Circuit
P0E44.description: P0E44 is the basic circuit code for the fifth pack voltage measurement, channel E, which follows channels A to D (P0ABA, P0B14, P0B19, P0B1E) in the code list. The battery controller stores it when this input is electrically unusable, for example open, without a plausible raw value or failing a self-test of its measuring stage, and none of the more specific low, high or erratic codes fits. No manufacturer documents P0E44 publicly, and which tap a maker labels E is its own decision. CARB requires every voltage sensor of the hybrid energy storage system to be monitored as an input component, with codes narrowing the fault down to a replaceable part. Without this value the controller restricts or blocks high-voltage operation.

causes.label: Open or unplugged voltage sense lead or connector inside the pack
Faulty measuring stage or input of the battery controller
Blown fuse or open resistor in the sense path

symptoms: Hybrid or high-voltage system warning lit
Reduced electric assist or limited battery power
Vehicle may not switch to ready mode

P0E45.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense E Circuit Range/Performance
P0E45.description: P0E45 says pack voltage measurement E delivers a value that is electrically valid but does not fit the rest of the battery data. Such a rationality test usually compares the channel with the summed block or cell voltages, or with a second pack measurement. No manufacturer documents P0E45 publicly. GM's 2013 two-mode hybrid trucks (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra) show the method on channel A: their battery pack control module fails P0ABB once the gap between pack voltage and the added-up block voltages exceeds 50 V in 70 of 80 checks taken every 100 ms, Type A, one trip. CARB requires plausibility monitoring for battery voltage sensors. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults of channel E are P0E44, P0E46, P0E47 and P0E48. Battery power is usually limited.

causes.label: Corroded or loose sense connection adding resistance and skewing the reading
Drifting measuring stage or outdated software in the battery controller
Fault in the reference value, e.g. a block or cell voltage channel

symptoms: Warning light with reduced hybrid or electric power
Displayed state of charge or range jumps unexpectedly

P0E46.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense E Circuit Low
P0E46.description: P0E46 is stored when pack voltage measurement E reads below the lowest value the connected battery could physically present. That points to the measuring path, such as a sense lead shorted to ground, a blown sense fuse or a failed input stage, not to an empty battery. No manufacturer documents P0E46 publicly. On GM's 2013 two-mode hybrid trucks the comparable channel A code P0ABC sets below 40 V, but only after the contactors have been closed for more than 200 ms, and needs 300 failures in 400 samples at 10 ms, Type A, one trip. CARB requires out-of-range checks for battery voltage sensors. The high counterpart is P0E47; a pack that is really deeply discharged sets its own codes such as P0AFA. Hybrid operation may be blocked.

causes.label: Sense lead of channel E shorted to ground or chassis
Blown fuse or open resistor in the sense path pulling the reading down
Defective input stage of the battery controller

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive or drops out of ready mode
Hybrid system warning and MIL lit
Electric drive or engine assist unavailable

P0E47.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense E Circuit High
