causes.label: Balancing circuit of unit F failed, cells overcharged
Measuring channel of unit F reading too high
Charger or regeneration control overshooting

symptoms: Charging refused or regenerative braking weak
MIL and battery warning

P0ED4.title: Generator Phase X Current
P0ED4.description: P0ED4 is the general current fault for phase X of the hybrid generator. J2012 names the generator phases U, V and W and adds a separate X, Y, Z series, which presumably serves machines with a second three-phase winding set fed by its own inverter bridge; which vehicles use it is not published, and no manufacturer documents P0ED4. Low and high cases are P0ED5 and P0ED6. Ford explains the role of its U-V-W codes on its 2019 power-split hybrids: the inverter is checked for overcurrent, current sensor and current regulation faults, and generator problems of this kind are stored as P0A6F, P0A72, P0A75 or their high variants. CARB requires electric drive components to be monitored. A faulty phase current limits generator output, engine start and charging.

causes.label: Fault in the inverter bridge or current regulation for phase X
Phase X current sensor out of tolerance
Loose or damaged high-voltage connection of phase X

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced charging, engine may start less smoothly

P0ED5.title: Generator Phase X Current Low
P0ED5.description: P0ED5 means that phase X of the hybrid generator carries, or appears to carry, too little current while the generator is supposed to deliver torque. No manufacturer documents P0ED5 publicly. Mitsubishi publishes a comparable check for the U, V and W phases of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: with at least 50 A requested and the generator between 500 and 4,500 rpm, a phase current that stays within roughly 17 A of zero for 0.4 s sets P0E0C, as does a failed comparison with the target current. In phase X the same result comes from a broken phase cable, a burnt winding joint, an inverter switch that never conducts, or a current sensor stuck at its zero point. P0ED6 is the high case; the low codes of phases Y and Z are P0ED8 and P0EDB. Generator torque and charging suffer.

causes.label: Open or loose phase X cable or terminal
Inverter power switch for phase X not conducting
Burnt or broken winding connection in the generator
Current sensor stuck near zero

symptoms: Weak or no battery charging by the generator
Rough engine start or vibration from the generator
MIL and hybrid warning

P0ED6.title: Generator Phase X Current High
P0ED6.description: P0ED6 is stored when the current in phase X of the hybrid generator exceeds its permitted limit. No manufacturer documents P0ED6 publicly. Ford gives figures for the comparable U, V and W codes P0A71, P0A74 and P0A77 on its 2019 power-split hybrids: the motor/generator control unit declares overcurrent once the generator current magnitude passes 300 A for 400 microseconds, or 15 A for 200 ms just after power-up, when practically no current should flow. Genuine overcurrent points to a winding short, damaged insulation or a power switch that fails closed; a current sensor with too much gain triggers a false alarm. The inverter shuts down to protect itself, so the hybrid system may stop working. Low side: P0ED5; general code: P0ED4.

causes.label: Turn-to-turn or ground short in the phase X winding
Inverter power switch failed closed
Current sensor reading too high (false overcurrent)

symptoms: Sudden hybrid system shutdown or loss of ready mode
MIL and hybrid warning

P0ED7.title: Generator Phase Y Current
P0ED7.description: P0ED7 is the general current code for phase Y, the middle phase of the generator's X-Y-Z set. Without being narrowed to low (P0ED8) or high (P0ED9), it says that the Y current no longer behaves as the inverter controller expects. No manufacturer documents P0ED7 publicly, and it is not known which production machines label their phases X, Y and Z. Ford describes what phase currents are used for in its 2019 hybrids: sensors on each phase feed the motor/generator control unit, which needs them to work out current magnitude and angle and also to confirm that the three AC cables are connected the right way. Monitoring of such electric drive parts is mandatory under CARB. Check the high-voltage connectors and look for other phase codes. Phase X: P0ED4, phase Z: P0EDA.

causes.label: Inverter fault affecting the phase Y bridge
Phase cables mixed up or poorly seated after repair work
Phase Y current sensor fault

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Limited generator operation

P0ED8.title: Generator Phase Y Current Low
P0ED8.description: P0ED8 reports too little current in phase Y of the hybrid generator. No manufacturer documents P0ED8 publicly. Ford's 2019 hybrid summary describes a phase circuit test at power-up for the U-V-W phases: the motor/generator control unit declares a phase circuit fault if less than 5 A is seen over the 100 ms test window. Seen this way, a low Y current is first of all a question of continuity: an open cable or terminal, a failed winding joint or an inverter switch that does not turn on. A sensor that reads too low would make the controller drive more real current than intended, so a low code from the sensor side deserves the same attention. Generator torque and charging power drop. High counterpart: P0ED9; same fault on phases X and Z: P0ED5, P0EDB.

causes.label: Open or corroded phase Y cable or terminal
Inverter switch for phase Y not turning on
Phase Y current sensor reading too low

symptoms: Generator delivers less charging power
Uneven running or noise from the transaxle
MIL and hybrid warning

P0ED9.title: Generator Phase Y Current High
P0ED9.description: P0ED9 is set when phase Y of the hybrid generator draws more current than allowed. No manufacturer documents P0ED9 publicly. Overcurrent in a generator phase is a protection event: the inverter must switch off within fractions of a millisecond, before its power semiconductors are destroyed. The scale is illustrated by Ford's limits for the U-V-W phases, 300 A for 400 microseconds in operation. Causes include a short between turns or to ground in the Y winding, a chafed phase cable and an inverter switch stuck on; a sensor that reads high can imitate the fault. If several phases report high at the same moment, the inverter or its common supply is more likely than three separate defects. Low side: P0ED8; the same fault on phase X: P0ED6.

causes.label: Short in the phase Y winding or to the housing
Inverter switch stuck on
Chafed phase cable shorting to ground
Current sensor reading too high

symptoms: Hybrid system shuts down, vehicle may lose ready mode
MIL and hybrid warning

P0EDA.title: Generator Phase Z Current
P0EDA.description: P0EDA is the general current fault of phase Z, the last of the three X-Y-Z generator phases, without the detail of P0EDB (low) or P0EDC (high). No manufacturer documents P0EDA publicly. In a three-phase set the currents add up to almost zero at every instant, so a controller can calculate one phase from the other two or use the sum as a cross-check; Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV, for instance, fails its generator sum check P0DFA when, with the switches off, the sum stays at 140 A or above for 0.35 s. A faulty Z current therefore often shows up together with sum or correlation faults. Under CARB these drive components must be supervised as well. Expect a hybrid system warning and limited generator operation. Phases X and Y: P0ED4, P0ED7.

causes.label: Phase Z current sensor offset or failure
Inverter fault on the phase Z bridge
Poor contact at the phase Z high-voltage terminal

symptoms: Hybrid warning, often with further phase or sum codes
Reduced charging and generator assist

P0EDB.title: Generator Phase Z Current Low
P0EDB.description: P0EDB means phase Z of the hybrid generator shows less current than the commanded operating point calls for. No manufacturer documents P0EDB publicly. Besides an absolute floor, published checks also look at the gap between actual and target current: Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV fails a U-V-W phase not only when it hovers near zero under demand but also when it misses its target current. If phase Z falls short, the machine runs unbalanced, which causes torque ripple, humming and extra heat in the remaining phases, so the inverter lowers generator power. Likely causes are a loose or corroded high-voltage terminal, a broken lead in the winding, a power switch that no longer conducts or a sensor offset. High counterpart: P0EDC; general code: P0EDA.

causes.label: Loose or corroded phase Z high-voltage terminal
Broken conductor in the phase Z winding
Power switch for phase Z no longer conducting
Phase Z current sensor offset

symptoms: Humming or vibration from the hybrid transaxle
Reduced generator power and charging
MIL and hybrid warning

P0EDC.title: Generator Phase Z Current High
P0EDC.description: P0EDC is the overcurrent code for phase Z of the hybrid generator and ends the X-Y-Z series. No manufacturer documents P0EDC publicly; the closest published logic is Ford's for its U-V-W generator phases (P0A71, P0A74, P0A77), which also flags any current above 15 A in the first 200 ms after power-up, a moment when the machine should be idle. A reading like that hints at a switch leaking or stuck on rather than at load. During operation a short between winding turns, an insulation fault to the housing, a damaged power module or a sensor with excessive gain can be behind the code; a sensor error usually also upsets the three-phase sum check. After the protective shutdown the generator no longer charges and electric engine starting may fail. Low side: P0EDB.

causes.label: Damaged or leaking power module for phase Z
Insulation fault or turn short in the phase Z winding
Current sensor with excessive gain

symptoms: Hybrid system shutdown, engine may not start
MIL and hybrid warning, possibly with sum check codes

P0EDD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack B Deterioration
P0EDD.description: P0EDD is the state-of-health verdict for the second section of a traction battery: section B has lost so much capacity or gained so much internal resistance that it falls below the maker's limit. P0A7F covers section A, P0EDE to P0EE1 sections C to F. Audi counts the Q5 PHEV (2020-2024) battery in groups and names P0EDD00 as group 2 deterioration in the battery management unit 008C; with the MIL on and guided fault finding silent, TSB 2079556/1 says to renew the module named by the entry. FCA uses the code on the Pacifica Hybrid: 08-299-25 extends warranty and replaces the 400 V pack, while a 2025 STAR case first checks fuses, wiring and BPCM software, then resets P0EDD in the BPCM. On the 2021 Wrangler, 08-168-23 calls it a false MIL fixed by BPCM software.

causes.label: Battery module or cell group in section B aged beyond its limit
Battery controller software misjudging state of health (FCA reflash cases)
Pack defect covered by a warranty extension (Pacifica Hybrid)

symptoms: MIL or hybrid system warning on
Noticeably shorter electric range
Engine runs more often, less electric assist

P0EDE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack C Deterioration
P0EDE.description: P0EDE flags the third battery section, C, as worn out. The controller estimates each section's usable capacity and resistance from voltage behaviour under load and at rest; if section C drifts too far from its new-state values, it is judged deteriorated. CARB asks for a state-of-health monitor and for codes that point to the smallest part a workshop can replace, which is why a multi-module pack gets one code per section. Only Audi documents P0EDE publicly: on the Q5 PHEV it stands for battery group 3 in control unit 008C. A February 2025 reporting obligation, 2076982/1, lists it with the yellow engine lamp and a displayed electric range that is too low, and asks dealers to call technical support before replacing parts. Sections B and D have P0EDD and P0EDF.

causes.label: Cells in battery group 3 aged (capacity loss, higher resistance)
Strong voltage spread inside the section
Controller estimate wrong, module still healthy

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Displayed electric range too low
Electric driving mode cannot be selected or ends early

P0EDF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack D Deterioration
P0EDF.description: P0EDF belongs to the fourth section of the traction battery. It is not a sensor or wiring code but a capacity and power judgement: the battery controller has concluded that section D can no longer deliver what the maker expects of a healthy unit. Audi maps P0EDF00 on the Q5 PHEV to battery group 4 in the battery management unit 008C. Its bulletin 2079556/1 of September 2025 describes the workshop path: the MIL is on, guided fault finding offers no measure, so the high-voltage module behind the stored entry is removed and a new one fitted; if more than two modules are flagged, a technical assistance ticket comes first. Other makers have not published the code. Because only one module is replaced, the cost is far below a full pack. P0EDE and P0EE0 cover the adjacent sections.

causes.label: High-voltage module of group 4 worn out
Single weak cell pulling the section down
Evaluation logic of the battery controller

symptoms: MIL on
Reduced electric range and power

P0EE0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack E Deterioration
P0EE0.description: With P0EE0 the controller reports ageing of section E, the fifth part of the traction battery. A section is usually a module or a group of cell blocks with its own monitoring; once its share of the pack has lost too much capacity or become too resistive, the whole battery can no longer reach its rated energy, which shows up first as shorter electric range. Audi is the only maker with published references: on the Q5 PHEV, P0EE000 means battery group 5 in unit 008C, and both the 2025 reporting obligation 2076982 and the module replacement bulletin 2079556 list it, intermittent or static. The first also names P0BBD, a voltage spread beyond the limit, which often goes along with a weak section. Distinguishing feature: only section E is named; sections D and F use P0EDF and P0EE1.

causes.label: Capacity loss of battery group 5
Cell voltages in the section spread too far (often with P0BBD)
Faulty state-of-health estimate

symptoms: Electric range shown too low
Engine warning lamp on
Less power in electric mode

P0EE1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack F Deterioration
P0EE1.description: P0EE1 is the last code of the P0E range for section ageing and covers section F. The series runs A (P0A7F) and B to F (P0EDD to P0EE1); for further sections J2012 continues in the P2 block, with G and H as P2CCC and P2CCD. Audi uses exactly this chain on the Q5 PHEV: groups 1 to 8 of the battery are reported as P0A7F00, P0EDD00 to P0EE100, P2CCC00 and P2CCD00 in unit 008C, and P0EE100 is group 6. The 2025 bulletins treat it like its siblings: confirm the MIL complaint, find no other measure in guided fault finding, replace the affected module. No other maker has published P0EE1. CARB's rule that fault codes should isolate the smallest replaceable unit explains why such long letter series exist for large packs. Section E is P0EE0.

causes.label: Module of battery group 6 aged
Section aged faster due to heat or poor cooling
Evaluation error of the battery controller

symptoms: MIL on
Shorter electric range

P0EE2.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Stuck/Open
P0EE2.description: P0EE2 says the second refrigerant distribution valve, B, stays open or fails to close. In plug-in hybrids and EVs such shut-off valves route refrigerant either to the cabin evaporator or to a chiller that cools the battery; Egelhof sells solenoid versions with 12 V or 24 V coils for exactly this use. The fault is inferred, since the module sees pressures or temperatures that would not occur with the valve shut. Audi documents it on the A7 55 TFSI e (2021-2023): P0EE200 is stored in thermal management unit J1024, address 00C5, and the MIL comes on. TSB 2071040/1 blames the J1024 software and lists an SVM update from container 4K8909476J/K/L to 4K8909476V; the HV charging cable must be unplugged during flashing. Valve A stuck open is P0EC9.

causes.label: Thermal management software misjudging the valve (Audi J1024)
Valve seat contaminated or armature stuck open
Weak coil that no longer moves the armature

symptoms: MIL on
Weaker cabin or battery cooling
Often no noticeable effect beyond the warning

P0EE3.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit/Open
P0EE3.description: P0EE3 concerns the wiring between the controlling module and refrigerant valve B, most often an interrupted path. With the output switched off, the driver normally sees a defined voltage through the coil; with it switched on, current flows. If neither picture appears, for instance because a pin has backed out of the connector or the coil winding is broken, the circuit is declared open. No manufacturer documents P0EE3 publicly. That valve B exists as a separately monitored part is shown by Audi's A7 PHEV, whose thermal management unit J1024 reports its mechanical fault as P0EE200. Typical hardware is a 12 V solenoid like Egelhof's shut-off valves. CARB requires every electronic output used for battery thermal management to be checked for open circuits. The matching valve A code is P2611.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the valve connector
Broken coil winding in valve B
Broken wire in the harness to the valve

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Valve B no longer switches, affected refrigerant branch stays as it is

P0EE4.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit Low
P0EE4.description: P0EE4 is stored when the control line of refrigerant valve B is pulled to a lower voltage than the driver commands, usually by a short to ground. With a high-side driver the valve would then stay energised or the output would be overloaded; with a low-side driver the coil may be switched on permanently. No manufacturer documents P0EE4 publicly. The closest published case is the valve A sibling P2612, which Ross-Tech describes for Volkswagen models as a short to ground at the N280 compressor regulator valve, a coil of about 10 ohms with a moulded connector that can turn brittle and let the pins corrode. A similar check on the valve B coil and its connector is a sensible start. Open and high faults of valve B are P0EE3 and P0EE5.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through to ground
Brittle or corroded valve connector
Coil winding shorted to the valve body

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Valve B behaves as if permanently energised or not at all

P0EE5.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit High
P0EE5.description: P0EE5 means the control line of refrigerant valve B carries more voltage than its commanded state allows. If the driver switches the coil to ground, a short to a 12 V feed is the classic reason; with some driver types an open coil can also float the line high. The practical effect depends on whether valve B is normally open or normally closed: either it cannot be energised any more, or it is energised when it should rest. No manufacturer documents P0EE5 publicly. Audi's A7 PHEV shows that valve B is watched by its own thermal management unit (J1024), and automotive shut-off valves of this kind run on 12 V or 24 V coils, according to Egelhof. CARB requires electrical checks of such battery thermal management outputs. P0EE4 is the low counterpart, P2613 the valve A code.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a 12 V feed
Open coil letting the line float high
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Cabin or battery cooling not working as requested

P0EE6.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P0EE6.description: P0EE6 is reported by the output stage itself: the switch that powers refrigerant valve B has measured too much current or got too hot and has protected itself. Modern smart high-side switches do this on chip; TI's TPS1HB16-Q1, for example, has an adjustable current limit between 4.4 and 49 A, shuts down at about 150 C junction temperature with roughly 20 C hysteresis, and flags the event on its diagnostic output. A coil drawing more current than normal, through shorted turns or a partial short in the wire, is the usual cause; a hot mounting spot of the module can add to it. No manufacturer documents P0EE6 publicly. Unlike P0EE4, the circuit still conducts and is not simply grounded. The same driver fault on valve A is P266F; Audi's A7 PHEV logs a valve B fault in J1024.

causes.label: Shorted turns in the valve B coil raising the current
Partial short in the valve wiring
Control module output stage overheating

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Valve B switched off, cooling branch not served

P0EE7.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor B Circuit
P0EE7.description: P0EE7 is the general circuit code for the second temperature sensor of the charging inlet. High-current inlets carry several sensors; the supplier Sailtran fits one PT1000 at the L1 pin and two independent PT1000 at DC+ and DC- of its CCS2 inlet, so A and B often stand for two different contacts. The code applies when the sensor B circuit is faulty in a way the module does not sort into low, high or implausible. No manufacturer documents P0EE7 on an official server. For sensor A, Mercedes lists P0D9900 as an electrical fault of the inlet contact sensor on the smart electric drive with 22 kW charger and traces it to loose low-voltage plugs at the charger (LI54.10-P-067823). CARB requires plug-in charger faults that stop or slow charging to be found. Sensor A is P0D99.

causes.label: Loose low-voltage connector between inlet and charger
Damaged sensor wire in the inlet harness
Failed sensor element B (usually means a new inlet)

symptoms: Charging refused or stopped
Charge indicator shows a fault

P0EE8.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0EE8.description: P0EE8 is set when sensor B in the charging inlet delivers an electrically valid value that does not fit the situation. A plausibility test may compare it with sensor A on the neighbouring pin, with the outside temperature after a long rest, or with the heating expected for the charge current. If B reads far colder than A during a high-current session, or shows a sudden rise without current, it fails. No manufacturer documents P0EE8 publicly. GM gives a hint for the A sensor equivalent P0D9A on the 2022 Hummer EV and BrightDrop EV600: worn or oversized terminals in public charge plugs are a suspect, and the test only runs again after about ten minutes of driving above 2 mph (PIT5904). Inlets with two DC pin sensors, as Sailtran builds them, make such a cross-check possible.

causes.label: Worn station plug heating one contact unevenly
Drifting sensor element B
Sensor B lost thermal contact to its pin

symptoms: Charging reduced or aborted
Fault only at certain stations

P0EE9.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
P0EE9.description: P0EE9 reports that the voltage of coupler temperature sensor B lies under its valid window. What that means thermally depends on the element. An NTC thermistor loses resistance when heated, so a low signal reads as an extremely hot pin. The PT1000 platinum sensors that Sailtran places at the DC+ and DC- contacts of its CCS2 inlet behave the other way round, and in a pull-up circuit a low signal looks implausibly cold. A short to ground pulls the line down with either type, and water in the inlet can do the same. No manufacturer documents P0EE9 publicly. Bentley's TPI 2075291/1 for the 2024 Bentayga Hybrid shows for sensor A that Low is P0D9B, even though the charger unit 00C6 showed the texts of Low and High swapped. P0EEA is the high-signal sibling.

causes.label: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Moisture or water in the charging inlet
Shorted sensor element B

symptoms: Charging not started or stopped
Reduced charging power

P0EEA.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
P0EEA.description: P0EEA is the opposite case: the sensor B signal of the charging inlet sits above the valid window. In a pull-up design that is what an unplugged connector, a broken sensor wire or a short to a supply voltage looks like. With a PT1000, whose resistance grows with heat, a high reading suggests an overheated contact, so the charger may stop at once; Sailtran fits PT1000 sensors at the DC+ and DC- pins of its CCS2 inlet. With an NTC it would read as far too cold, which hides real heating and is no safer. No manufacturer documents P0EEA publicly. For the A sensor, Bentley confirms on the 2024 Bentayga Hybrid that High is P0D9C and warns that the charger unit showed the wrong text, so diagnosis must follow the code number. P0EE9 is the low-signal sibling.

causes.label: Unplugged connector or broken sensor B wire
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open sensor element B inside the inlet

symptoms: Charging aborted at once or refused
Fault in the charge indicator

P0EEB.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0EEB.description: P0EEB catches a sensor B signal from the charging inlet that jumps or drops out for moments. A metal contact and its plastic housing have real thermal mass, so a change of many degrees within milliseconds cannot be a true temperature and points to the circuit. No manufacturer documents P0EEB publicly. A Mercedes bulletin about the first inlet sensor of the third-generation smart with its optional 22 kW unit fits the pattern: inlet sensor codes there came from loose low-voltage contacts at the charger, the fix was to work the plugs gently and watch whether charging starts, and the bulletin warns the fault may only appear with warm or cold parts at the start or end of charging. Typical for P0EEB is a session that stops without visible reason and works next time. Steady faults are P0EE9 and P0EEA.

causes.label: Loose contact in the sensor B circuit or at the charger plug
Moisture that comes and goes in the inlet connector
Cracked sensor element with temperature-dependent contact

symptoms: Charging stops sporadically
Fault cannot be reproduced at once

P0EEC.title: Battery Energy Control Module B Performance
P0EEC.description: P0EEC says a second battery energy control module, B, has failed its own internal checks. Large or split packs can carry more than one such controller, each watching cell voltages, temperatures and current of its part. No manufacturer documents P0EEC publicly. GM shows how the module A version P0A1F works: in its 2016 and 2019 hybrid tables a single software watchdog reset of the controller is enough, checked at 9 V or more, and the code is Type A, so the MIL lights after one trip. That a B module exists in practice is visible at Audi: on the Q5 and A7 PHEV, U041300 reports invalid data from Battery Energy Control Module B, and TSB 2065722/2 links it to software 106 or 206 in the battery junction box SX6. Network loss of the module is a U code; P0A1F covers module A.

causes.label: Software fault or watchdog reset in module B
Low or unstable 12 V supply to the module
Internal hardware fault of module B

symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning on
Limited electric drive or charging

P0EED.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Discharge Circuit Performance
P0EED.description: P0EED concerns the active discharge path on the high-voltage side, the circuit that drains the DC link capacitors once the contactors have opened so that no dangerous voltage lingers. The code says this path does not perform as intended, whereas P0C76 only judges how long the voltage takes to fall. FCA lists P0EED-00 for the 2017 Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid in bulletin 08-107-17, next to P0C76, P0C77 and P0AFA: a loose terminal bolt where the high-voltage lead joins the inverter module (PIM) could arc, the MIL came on and propulsion might be lost. Repair was a torque check to 25 N·m, or a new inverter module and cable if arcing marks were found. As a reference for the timing side, GM's P0C76 fails when the inverter still reads above 200 V 3.5 s after opening, Type A.

causes.label: Loose or arcing high-voltage cable terminal at the inverter module (FCA 08-107-17)
Discharge resistor or its switching transistor open or degraded
Internal fault in the inverter or its voltage measurement
Main contactor sticking closed so the bus stays charged

symptoms: MIL or hybrid system warning on
Loss of propulsion or vehicle will not enter ready mode
Further high-voltage codes such as P0C76 or P0C77 stored at the same time

P0EEE.title: Battery Charger Coupler Temperature B Too High
P0EEE.description: P0EEE is the overheating verdict for the second measuring point of the charging inlet: sensor B works electrically, but the contact it watches has become too hot, so charging is throttled or stopped. Electrical faults of sensor B have their own codes P0EE7 to P0EEB; overheating at point A is P0E5F, at points C and D P2E4E and P2E53. Ford documents P0EEE in special service message 55080 for certain Mustang Mach-E (2021 to 2023), E-Transit (2022 to 2025) and F-150 Lightning (2022 to 2023): DC fast charging at level 3 stations breaks off, and the vehicle stores P0EEE:27 together with P2E53:27 in the SOBDM. Ford traces this to module software, says a new charge port does not cure it and expects a software fix in Q3 2026; AC charging keeps working. Outside this case, worn or dirty pins are the usual cause.

causes.label: Software of the charging diagnostic module misjudging the temperature (Ford SSM 55080)
Worn, dirty or corroded pins in the charging inlet
Loose crimp or screw connection behind the inlet pin raising contact resistance
Worn plug of the charging station heating the contact

symptoms: DC fast charging stops or does not start
Charging power reduced while AC charging still works
Charging fault message in the cluster or app

P0EEF.title: Drive Motor A Control Module Overtemperature
P0EEF.description: P0EEF reports that the control module of drive motor A, the inverter electronics that switch the motor phases, has run too hot. The temperature reading itself is considered valid; faults of the inverter temperature sensors, such as P0AEF, are separate codes. No manufacturer documents P0EEF publicly. GM gives an idea of the limits on the 2016 Volt: its motor control processor A sets P0C11, P0C12 or P0C13 when power inverter phase U, V or W stays above 126 °C for 1.2 s within a 2 s window, rated Type A with the MIL after one trip. CARB demands that hybrid systems monitor electric motor performance. Low coolant in the electronics loop, a weak coolant pump, trapped air or long heavy load in hot weather heat the module, which then reduces motor torque to protect itself.

causes.label: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Electronics coolant pump weak or failed
Long full-load operation such as towing or climbing in high ambient heat
Degraded power semiconductors or thermal interface inside the module

symptoms: Reduced drive power or hybrid system warning
MIL on (manufacturer-dependent)
Electric drive switched off until the module cools

P0EF0.title: Battery Charger Coupler Unlock Disabled - High Voltage Present
P0EF0.description: P0EF0 describes a safety lockout rather than a broken actuator: the vehicle keeps the charging connector locked because it still measures hazardous voltage at the inlet. CharIN's CCS design guide permits unlocking only below 60 V, and EVgo's interoperability guide for vehicle makers asks for release once current is close to zero, the inlet is under 60 V DC and the station has changed to state B1. If the voltage does not decay, for instance because a DC charging contactor has welded, the station leaves its output live or the vehicle's voltage measurement is wrong, the lock stays engaged and the code is logged. No manufacturer documents P0EF0 publicly. Electrical faults of the lock actuator are P0D91 to P0D98. The driver cannot remove the cable until the voltage is gone.

causes.label: DC charging contactor stuck closed, inlet stays connected to the battery
Charging station does not switch off or discharge its output
Faulty inlet voltage measurement reporting voltage that is not there
Charging control software ending the session in the wrong order

symptoms: Charging cable cannot be unplugged after charging
Charging fault message, sometimes only at certain stations
Emergency release of the connector needed

P0EF1.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0EF1.description: P0EF1 is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor of drive motor C, the third traction motor on vehicles with three or more electric machines. It must not be confused with P2DB1, which means sensor C inside drive motor A. Volvo Trucks lists P0EF1 with failure type 09, component failure, for its electric trucks in remote diagnostic bulletin RD21-022; it names connector, wiring harness, the motor temperature sensor itself and an unsupported configuration as possible causes and sends the technician to Tech Tool for the detailed steps. The general code is used when the fault is not classified as low or high, which have their own codes P0EF3 and P0EF4. Without a usable winding temperature the controller has to protect motor C and limits its output.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or damaged connector of the motor C temperature sensor
Chafed or broken sensor wiring
Temperature sensor in the winding failed
Controller configuration not matching the installed motor (Volvo RD21-022)

symptoms: Reduced drive power
Warning lamp for the electric drive
Motor temperature shown as invalid in the scan tool

P0EF2.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0EF2.description: P0EF2 flags a plausibility error of the drive motor C temperature sensor: its signal is electrically fine, yet the value does not fit what the controller expects. No manufacturer documents P0EF2 publicly. GM shows a typical check for drive motor B on the 2016 Cadillac ELR: after at least 21,600 s with the propulsion system inactive, the motor thermistor may differ by no more than 20 °C from the average of power electronics coolant and transmission fluid temperature, otherwise P0A31 sets as Type A. Ford compares motor coil, generator coil and transmission fluid temperatures on its 2019 hybrids after 200 minutes key-off, with limits of 10 °C and 30 °C. A drifting thermistor, a sensor that has lost contact with the winding or a high-resistance connection fails such a cold-start comparison.

causes.label: Thermistor characteristic drifted with age
Sensor no longer in thermal contact with the winding
Corroded pin adding resistance and shifting the reading
Comparison sensor such as coolant or oil temperature reading wrong

symptoms: Warning lamp after a long standstill, often at the first start of the day
Usually no noticeable drivability change at first
Power limitation of motor C in some cases

P0EF3.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0EF3.description: P0EF3 is stored when the signal voltage of the drive motor C temperature sensor drops below its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor on a pull-up resistor, a low voltage stands for an extremely hot winding, so electrically the suspects are a short to ground, a pinched harness or a sensor with an internal short. No manufacturer documents P0EF3 publicly. GM's motor B table for the 2016 Cadillac ELR shows the analogous limit: P0A32 trips once the reading corresponds to more than 184 °C, close to 0 V, after a 90 s warm-up, Type A. Ford's 2019 hybrids fail the motor coil sensor below 0.1 V held for 32 ms. Because the controller cannot tell such a short from real overheating, it derates motor C. P0EF4 covers the high-voltage side.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground or motor housing
Thermistor shorted internally
Water or coolant in the connector bridging the pins

symptoms: Drive power of motor C reduced immediately
Implausibly high motor temperature in the live data
Warning lamp on

P0EF4.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0EF4.description: P0EF4 reports a drive motor C temperature signal above the plausible window. For an NTC sensor on a pull-up this equals an impossibly cold winding, the picture produced by an open sensor, a broken wire, an unplugged connector or a short to the reference voltage. No manufacturer documents P0EF4 publicly. GM's ELR motor controller treats the same situation for motor B as P0A33 once the value reads below −41 °C, near 5 V, while Ford flags the coil sensor of its 2019 hybrids once the voltage exceeds 4.8 V for 32 ms. A sensor that claims far too low a temperature would hide real overheating, so the controller switches to a substitute value and limits the output of motor C. Check the connector at the motor first; the low-side sibling is P0EF3.

causes.label: Sensor connector unplugged, loose or with pushed-back pin
Broken signal or ground wire of the sensor
Thermistor open internally
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference

symptoms: Reduced power of motor C
Motor temperature stuck at the lowest value in the live data
Warning lamp on

P0EF5.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0EF5.description: P0EF5 covers a drive motor C temperature signal that jumps or drops out for short moments instead of staying wrong. Because of the thermal mass of a traction motor, the winding temperature can only change slowly; a step of many degrees within milliseconds therefore points to the wiring and not to the motor. Loose or corroded pins at the motor connector, leads chafing near moving parts or a cracked sensor lead are typical. No manufacturer documents P0EF5 publicly, and its drive motor A and B siblings P0A2E and P0A34 are not listed in the published Ford and GM tables either; Ford only runs open and short checks on its coil sensors with a 200 ms monitoring window. CARB requires hybrid systems to watch electric motor performance. Warnings that appear and vanish, sometimes with brief power cuts, are typical.

causes.label: Loose or corroded pins in the motor connector
Harness chafing at brackets or moving parts
Cracked sensor lead inside the motor that opens with vibration or heat

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short power interruptions of motor C, often on rough roads
Jumping motor temperature in the live data

P0EF6.title: Drive Motor C Temperature Sensor Over Temperature
P0EF6.description: P0EF6 is not an electrical fault: the drive motor C temperature sensor delivers a believable value, but that value has passed the motor's protection limit. No manufacturer documents P0EF6 publicly. For motor B on the 2016 Cadillac ELR, GM sets P0A35 when the temperature exceeds 149 °C and does not fall back below a reset threshold, Type A, and only while the range check P0A31 is passing. Ford's 2019 hybrids set P0A2F at a coil temperature above 140 °C or transmission oil above 115 °C. Causes are mostly on the cooling side, such as low coolant or oil, a failed pump or a clogged cooler, but long full-load phases or a winding with shorted turns also heat the motor. Torque of motor C is cut until it cools; sensor circuit faults belong to P0EF1 to P0EF5.

causes.label: Low coolant or oil level, or air in the motor cooling circuit
Failed coolant or oil pump, or clogged cooler
Long full-load phases such as towing, track use or steep climbs
Shorted turns in the stator winding generating extra heat

symptoms: Clearly reduced power until the motor has cooled down
Warning about drive system overheating
MIL on (manufacturer-dependent)

P0EF7.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor B Circuit
P0EF7.description: P0EF7 stands for an electrical fault in the second input voltage sensor of on-board charger A, the measuring channel that reads the AC supply voltage coming from a wallbox, station or household outlet. Chargers designed for several phases or split-phase supply may carry more than one such channel; the first one, sensor A, uses P0D3D to P0D41. This general code applies when the signal is unusable but not classified as range, low or high, which are P0EF8, P0EF9 and P0EFA. No manufacturer documents P0EF7 publicly. In its 2019 plug-in hybrid tables GM reads sensor A through a pulse duty ratio, so a broken line shows up as a stuck 0 % or 100 %. CARB requires plug-in vehicles to monitor charging system performance. As long as the supply voltage cannot be confirmed, AC charging is refused or limited.

causes.label: Fault in the voltage sensing stage inside the charger
Open or high-resistance signal line between sensor and controller
Corroded low-voltage connector at the charger

symptoms: AC charging does not start or stops shortly after start
Charging fault message in the cluster or app
DC fast charging usually unaffected

P0EF8.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0EF8.description: P0EF8 is set when input voltage sensor B of charger A delivers a value that is electrically valid but wrong for the situation. No manufacturer documents P0EF8 publicly. GM's rationality test for sensor A, P0D3E in its 2019 plug-in hybrid tables, illustrates the idea: while the car moves at 16 km/h or more, when no plug can be connected, the sensor duty ratio must stay between 8 and 12 %; if 60 of 80 samples taken every 25 ms fall outside, the code is stored as Type B. A charger with two input channels can additionally compare them with each other or with the supply voltage reported by the station. Offset drift or a partial fault in the sensing electronics is the likely cause, wiring less so. Charging may stop or continue at reduced power.

causes.label: Offset drift of the voltage sensing electronics in the charger
Partial internal fault of the charger input stage
Charger software misjudging the plausibility window

symptoms: AC charging interrupted or slower than expected
Code may set while driving without any charging attempt
Charging fault message

P0EF9.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor B Circuit Low
P0EF9.description: P0EF9 means the signal of input voltage sensor B in charger A has fallen below its valid range. No manufacturer documents P0EF9 publicly. GM's 2019 plug-in hybrid summary fails the matching sensor A code P0D3F when the duty cycle is 8 % or less but above zero, or stuck at 100 %, in at least 30 samples out of a window of 40 (Type B); a short to ground or a missing sensor supply produce that picture. Note that low refers to the measurement signal and not to a weak mains supply, which manufacturers report with input voltage too low codes such as P0D27. Because the charger cannot verify the incoming voltage, it does not begin AC charging. The high-side counterpart is P0EFA, the general circuit code P0EF7.

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to ground
Missing supply voltage of the sensing circuit
Internal fault of the charger measuring stage

symptoms: AC charging refused
Charging fault message right after plugging in
DC fast charging usually still possible

P0EFA.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor B Circuit High
P0EFA.description: With P0EFA, the signal from the second input voltage sensor of charger A, sensor B, lies above the plausible window. No manufacturer documents P0EFA publicly. GM's comparable check for sensor A, P0D40 in its 2019 plug-in hybrid tables, trips at a duty cycle of 92 % or more but below 100 %, or at exactly 0 %, in 30 of 40 samples, and is rated Type B. Electrically this points to a short to a supply voltage, an open signal line pulled up by the input stage, or a defective sensing stage inside the charger. Since the measuring channel normally sits on the charger board, the charger itself becomes the prime suspect once plugs and pins have been checked. AC charging is refused or ends soon after it started; the low-side sibling is P0EF9.

causes.label: Defective measuring stage on the charger board
Open signal line pulled high by the input circuit
Signal shorted to a supply voltage

symptoms: AC charging refused or ends after a few seconds
Charging fault message
Indicated charging power implausible

P0EFB.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor C Circuit
P0EFB.description: P0EFB flags an electrical fault on the third AC input voltage channel of on-board charger A, sensor C. Channel A reports through P0D3D to P0D41, channel B through P0EF7 to P0EFA; a third channel fits chargers that read each phase of a three-phase supply separately. This is the catch-all circuit code, used when the signal is unusable without being sorted into range, low or high (P0EFC, P0EFD, P0EFE). No manufacturer documents P0EFB publicly, and GM's hybrid tables for 2011, 2012 and 2014 to 2019 never list the matching circuit code P0D3D either, catching wiring faults on sensor A only through its low and high checks. In TI's 11 kW reference design every phase is scaled by a resistor chain and centred at 1.65 V in a 3.3 V converter, so a dead channel is easy to spot. AC charging is refused or limited.

causes.label: Failed measuring channel C on the charger board (divider, amplifier or converter input)
Open or loose sense connection for this phase inside the charger or at the AC inlet harness
Charger software marking a valid channel as faulty

symptoms: AC charging does not start or is limited
Possible reduced charging power on three-phase stations
Charging fault shown in the cluster or app

P0EFC.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P0EFC.description: With P0EFC, sensor C of charger A delivers an electrically sound signal whose value conflicts with the charger's other readings. No manufacturer documents P0EFC publicly. For sensor A, GM shows such a cross-check on the 2011 Volt: the charger module compares the AC peak voltage with two independent bulk voltage readings, and if both differ by more than 34 V for 512 ms within 640 ms, P0D3E is stored as Type A. GM preliminary information PIC5803 (Volt 2011 to 2013, Spark EV 2014) adds a warning: P0D3E together with P1E00 after an interrupted charge usually came from a brown-out, a power cut or a faulty cord set, not from the car. CARB likewise does not demand detection of faults that look the same as a weak supply. Check the outlet and station before blaming the charger.

causes.label: Voltage dips, brown-out or power cut at the outlet or station during charging (GM PIC5803 for the sensor A code)
Faulty or poorly calibrated charging cord set or wallbox
Gain or offset drift of measuring channel C in the charger
Charger software needing an update

symptoms: Charging stops part-way or does not reach full charge
Fault appears only at certain outlets or stations
Charging fault message, sometimes with a warning lamp

P0EFD.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor C Circuit Low
P0EFD.description: P0EFD reports that the reading of input voltage sensor C in charger A sits below its plausible band. No manufacturer documents P0EFD publicly. GM's 2011 Volt charger module gives a reference for sensor A: once AC is detected at the inlet, a peak value under 90 V for 1500 ms within a 1875 ms window sets P0D3F, Type A with the warning lamp after one trip. Causes on the measuring side are a short to ground on the sense path, a shorted lower divider resistor or a missing reference for the converter. A phase that is genuinely dead at the supply, such as a tripped breaker on one leg of a three-phase station, can produce the same picture, so the incoming voltage is measured first. Mains undervoltage proper has its own codes such as P0D27; the high counterpart is P0EFE.

causes.label: One phase missing at the supply (tripped breaker or fault in the station or cable)
Sense path of channel C shorted to ground
Defective divider or converter input for channel C in the charger

symptoms: AC charging refused right after plugging in
Charging works on a different station or outlet
Charging fault message

P0EFE.title: Battery Charger A Input Voltage Sensor C Circuit High
P0EFE.description: P0EFE is stored when channel C of charger A reports more input voltage than a household or station supply can deliver. No manufacturer documents P0EFE publicly. For sensor A, GM's 2011 Volt charger module trips P0D40 when the measured AC peak exceeds 422 V for 160 ms of a 200 ms window, rated Type A; this window is far shorter than the one for the low code, presumably because overvoltage endangers the input stage. In a divider front end like the one in TI's 11 kW design, an open lower resistor or a short to the converter reference pushes the signal toward the 3.3 V limit and causes exactly this reading. Real overvoltage from the grid is rare, so the measuring channel inside the charger is the main suspect once plugs have been checked. AC charging stops at once.

causes.label: Open lower resistor in the voltage divider of channel C
Sense signal shorted to the converter reference or a supply rail
Actual overvoltage or surge from the supply

symptoms: AC charging stops within seconds of starting
Displayed supply voltage unrealistically high
Charging fault message
